papers.llm_summary: Giới thiệu ReMAS, framework red-teaming hộp đen dùng RL để tấn công trích xuất system prompt của các sub-agent trong hệ thống multi-agent, có tính transferability.
papers.llm_reason: Core agent/security với experiment đầy đủ; cho insight an toàn MAS để làm content cảnh báo và bảo vệ agent mình dùng, nhưng ít gắn business/marketing trực tiếp.

papers.title: Hidden Messages Between Diffusion Language Model Agents: Causal Evidence for Latent Communication
papers.abstract: Diffusion language models form answers through a sequence of revisable continuous states, but multi-agent systems usually discard those states and make agents communicate only after decoding text. We ask whether one independent diffusion trajectory can pass a compact hidden message into another and, crucially, whether the receiver uses what that message means. In Hidden Messages, a sender compresses its denoising state into four signed dense vectors; the receiver consumes them while retaining its own context, canvas, and trajectory. Removing a message tests whether the channel matters; replacing it with a message from another example tests whether its content matters. Across controlled tasks, derangement removes a +63.6-point advantage on Tiny-A2D and a +100.0-point advantage on Dream-7B, while targeted substitutions steer the receiver toward the substituted fact. On QASC with the two supporting facts split across agents, matched communication reaches 80.8%, but a wrong-example message lowers accuracy to 46.8%, a content effect of +34.0 points. The surprising result is temporal: one late transfer reaches 87.8%, exceeding four recurrent exchanges by +7.0 points. These experiments provide causal evidence for continuous hidden communication between diffusion-LM agents and show that when information is transferred can matter more than how many times agents exchange it.
papers.llm_summary: Chứng minh因果扩散 LM agents có thể truyền hidden continuous messages cho nhau, và thời điểm truyền quan trọng hơn số lần trao đổi.
papers.llm_reason: Multi-agent communication core, experiment causal rõ ràng, insight 'timing > frequency' áp dụng được cho agent workflow, nhưng diffusion LM còn niche.

papers.title: UniGFM-RAG: Unify Graph Foundation Models and Large Language Models for End-to-End Retrieval and Reasoning
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown remarkable capabilities across tasks, but they still struggle with complex reasoning that requires integrating scattered knowledge. Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) addresses this challenge by organizing fragment knowledge as graphs, while recent Graph Foundation Models (GFMs) further improve GraphRAG with graph-native retrieval and reasoning capabilities. However, existing GraphRAG methods usually adopt decoupled retrieve-then-generate pipelines, which create objective misalignment between retrieval and reasoning, and training GFM retrievers typically depends on expensive human annotations. To address these limitations, we propose \ourmethod, a unified end-to-end GraphRAG framework that tightly couples a GFM retriever with an LLM generator. Given a query, the GFM retriever first reasons over the graph to score and retrieve relevant document nodes. These node embeddings are then passed through a fully differentiable graph bridge, which projects them into soft-weighted graph prefixes according to retrieval scores and combines them with raw document texts to form graph-augmented prompts. In this way, structural information is injected directly into LLM generation, while the final answer loss can be back-propagated through the bridge to jointly optimize retrieval and reasoning. To stabilize training and reduce reliance on costly annotations, we further introduce a semantic-guided distillation module that provides auxiliary supervision using pseudo-labels derived from query-document semantic similarities. Extensive experiments on three multi-hop QA datasets and three out-of-domain GraphRAG benchmarks show that \ourmethod consistently outperforms strong baseline methods and generalizes well, which demonstrates the effectiveness of end-to-end GraphRAG with tightly integrated GFM retrieval and LLM reasoning.
papers.llm_summary: UniGFM-RAG ghép Graph Foundation Model retriever với LLM generator trong một pipeline GraphRAG end-to-end, tối ưu chung retrieval và reasoning qua graph bridge.
papers.llm_reason: Rõ ràng AI/RAG cốt lõi (28), có pipeline train end-to-end (18), GraphRAG hữu ích cho knowledge-base content (10), nhưng thiên về kiến trúc nghiên cứu, khó làm ngay ohne infra (13).

papers.title: IntelliAudit: Using Large Language Models to Evaluate Audit Controls
papers.abstract: IT audits require auditors to judge whether heterogeneous organizational evidence satisfies semantic security and compliance controls. This judgment is difficult to automate because relevant evidence is distributed across policies, records, spreadsheets, and operational artifacts, and because audit conclusions depend on evidentiary sufficiency rather than keyword matching. We present IntelliAudit, a retrieval-grounded multi-agent system for IT audit evidence evaluation. Given a control and an evidence corpus, IntelliAudit retrieves relevant artifacts, generates an evidence-grounded assessment, challenges adverse findings, adjudicates disagreements, and produces an auditor-facing recommendation with cited evidence, rationale, missing-evidence analysis, and remediation guidance. We instantiate IntelliAudit on ISO/IEC 27001 and evaluate it across multiple simulated organizations using expert auditor review and audit-readiness user feedback. The evaluation shows that IntelliAudit can support control interpretation, evidence-grounded reasoning, and audit-preparation workflows, while also revealing the importance of human oversight for calibrating sufficiency judgments and correcting overly permissive recommendations. These results suggest that retrieval-grounded multi-agent systems can assist audit evidence review, but should remain decision-support tools rather than autonomous certification systems.
papers.llm_summary: IntelliAudit, multi-agent retrieval-grounded đánh giá evidence audit ISO/IEC 27001, tạo recommendation có trích dẫn, phân tích thiếu evidence và remediation guidance.
papers.llm_reason: Core multi-agent với evaluation expert review; gần business nhất (audit/compliance workflow), insight decision-support + human oversight áp dụng được cho content和业务 quyết định.

papers.title: Secure and Functional Code Generation with Self-Evaluation
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate functionally correct code that remains insecure. Security-focused fine-tuning can be expensive and is not always available, motivating inference-time approaches. Security-oriented prompting and retrieval can reduce vulnerabilities, but may also remove required behavior or apply defenses incompatible with the task. The challenge is to identify relevant security knowledge and use it to improve security without sacrificing functionality. We present SecGent, an inference-time framework that retrieves weakness context from the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) database and applies it to secure code generation. By connecting task specifications to relevant textual CWE records, SecGent provides task-specific security guidance without relying on retrieved vulnerable or patched code examples. Complementary functional and security tests check the resulting implementation, and their execution feedback guides repairs toward satisfying both objectives. We evaluate SecGent with four open-source LLMs and Claude Sonnet 5.5 across five programming languages on the CWEval benchmark. It achieves the highest joint functional--security success against four inference-time baselines for all five models. Across the open-weight models, mean functional-security@1 (FS@1) improves by 15.5% over RAG, with gains in both functionality and security, and by 19.8% over the strongest prompt optimizer compiled for each model. On Sonnet, FS@1 reaches 92.1%, outperforming the strongest baseline AutoGen by 4.8%. In a separate comparison, SecGent outperforms Claude Code with security-focused prompting by over 6% in FS@1. Feedback-guided repair further improves FS@1 by up to 6.7% over generation without feedback, primarily by recovering functionality while checking security.
papers.llm_summary: SecGent là framework inference-time truy xuất ngữ cảnh bảo mật từ CWE database để sinh code an toàn mà vẫn đảm bảo chức năng, vượt baseline trên 5 model và 5 ngôn ngữ lập trình.
papers.llm_reason: AI sinh code + bảo mật là topic nóng, có benchmark CWEval thật với nhiều model, nhưng ứng dụng trực tiếp vào content business của solopreneur chỉ ở mức trung bình.

papers.title: Agentic-ZTA: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Autonomous Zero Trust Enforcement
papers.abstract: Agentic AI is emerging as a promising paradigm for automating complex cybersecurity decisions, yet its use in enforcing zero trust introduces significant challenges in safety, reliability, and policy compliance. This paper presents Agentic AI based zero trust architecture (Agentic-ZTA) that operationalizes the NIST SP 800-207 ZTA architecture control loop through coordinated multi- agent decision pipeline. In the proposed framework, policy knowledge is embedded into a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline and retrieved at inference time as top-k relevant policies. Access requests are intercepted by the Policy Enforcement Point (PEP), enriched with contextual metadata. The request context is routed to a policy engine agent which invokes domain-specialized core agents first followed by supporting agents, if further evaluation needed. AI agents reason over access context, policy constraints and determine trust. The retrieved policies are embedded into agent prompt during inference time and agentic trust scores are aggregated and evaluated by a trust-algorithm, producing the final access decision for enforcement under continuous verification. We implement Agentic-ZTA in a testbed and evaluate it on representative access-control use cases scenarios. Our Agentic-ZTA framework achieves 95.0% accuracy, 93.9% precision, and 96.3% recall, and demonstrate the feasibility of enforcing zero trust using AI agents.
papers.llm_summary: Xây Agentic-ZTA: multi-agent pipeline với RAG policy NIST 800-207 để tự động quyết định zero-trust, đạt 95% accuracy, 93,9% precision, 96,3% recall trên testbed.
papers.llm_reason: Agent + core AI nhưng thiên cybersecurity (27), testbed có số liệu cụ thể (19), ít giá trị marketing/content (7), insight vai trò policy-agent & trust-score chỉ áp dụng nếu làm product bảo mật (14).

papers.title: CodeMeepo: A Multi-Agent Workflow for Repository-Level Code Migration and Optimization
papers.abstract: Repository-level code migration rewrites an entire project in a new programming language while preserving its observable behavior. It is challenging because behavior spans interdependent modules, dependencies and build infrastructure must be adapted to the target ecosystem, and the source code is often the only specification. Large language model agents can now attempt these migrations end to end, but three challenges remain. First, an agent that writes both the translation and its acceptance tests may overlook the same requirements in both, leaving missing or incorrect behavior undetected. Second, large repositories can exceed a model's context window, and dividing the work into smaller tasks does not ensure that all required behavior is migrated. Third, even behaviorally correct translations may be slower than the original implementation. We present CodeMeepo, a multi-agent pipeline for complete and efficient migration of large repositories. Each milestone is evaluated against a fixed external oracle that the agents neither author nor modify. A separate parity assessment compares source and target components in scope and adds identified gaps back into the plan as required work. Ordered milestones limit the scope of each task, while cumulative regression checks guard against breaking already-migrated behavior. A benchmark-guided optimization phase addresses performance, followed by full-suite conformance testing and repair. Eight specialized agent roles communicate through file artifacts, and a deterministic state machine governs repair, deferral, scope changes, and termination. On nine subjects in three language pairs, CodeMeepo achieves the best pass rate on every subject and passes 18% more tests than a state-of-the-art multi-agent baseline using the same model. On a production daemon, its optimization phase improves half of the benchmarks, by 25% on average.
papers.llm_summary: CodeMeepo pipeline multi-agent migrate toàn repo sang ngôn ngữ mới với external oracle cố định, parity assessment, milestone ordering và benchmark-guided optimization.
papers.llm_reason: Multi-agent workflow mạnh, pattern (oracle ngoài, regression) có thể học cho agent content, nhưng domain code migration xa content marketing.

papers.title: A Framework for Identifying, Categorizing, and Explaining Bias in AI-Generated Code
papers.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become integrated into software development workflows, concerns regarding unintentional biases in AI-generated code. Although evidence suggests these biases exist, limited research has systematically identified, categorized, and explained them. This study investigates bias in AI-generated code and evaluates whether LLMs can reliably identify and explain it through a taxonomy-driven framework. We extended an existing dataset of biased AI-generated Python code and manually annotated snippets with bias categories and human-authored justifications to establish a ground-truth dataset. Using this dataset, we evaluated proprietary and open-source LLMs as automated bias detection and justification systems through ICL. Finally, we analyzed similarity between LLM-generated explanations and human-authored justifications using structured justification and code identification metrics. Our findings demonstrate that LLMs can effectively support code bias identification and explanation. Gemini achieved 80.14% classification accuracy, with 84.0% precision and 95.7% recall, while the best open-source alternative, Qwen3-coder, achieved 82.45% accuracy, 68.64% precision, and 80.22% recall. Additionally, the models achieved justification similarity scores of 80.4% and 80.14%, respectively, relative to human-authored reasoning, and code identification similarity scores of 86.0% and 87.82%. These results suggest that LLMs can detect biased logic in generated Python code and produce explanations that substantially align with expert interpretations.
papers.llm_summary: Framework taxonomy để LLM phát hiện và giải thích bias trong code AI sinh (Gemini 80.14%, Qwen3-coder 82.45%).
papers.llm_reason: Core LLM-for-code + evaluation thật với metrics rõ; có thể làm góc content 'AI code có bias' và dùng LLM kiểm duyệt code, nhưng business/marketing relevance trung bình.

papers.title: TRACE: Governing Memory Validity in Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Persistent memory lets language-model agents carry information across long-running collaborations, but leaves a lifecycle question open: what may a returning agent still act on once the shared state has changed? A memory can be correctly retrieved, relevant to the current task, and faithful to its source, and nonetheless be inadmissible for action: an itinerary saved before a pause still names the hotel the team has since replaced. We formalize this as temporal memory admission and present TRACE, a training-free layer that treats re-entry as an eligibility decision rather than a storage or retrieval operation, reconciling a departure checkpoint against absence-period updates, resolving explicit and implicit invalidation, and releasing a bounded Return View only when it covers the returning role's open obligations. We evaluate TRACE under three actor models on Memora, STALE Type II, and a derived ManBench-Return setting, each recast as return episodes: one agent departs, four teammates change the shared state, and the agent rejoins. What separates methods is not overall accuracy but whether one can retain valid memory and reject stale memory at once, and no single-policy baseline can: Restore (reinstate the departure checkpoint in full) admits stale state, Reset (start the return from an empty memory) discards valid state, each bottoming out at 0% on one of the two. TRACE is the only method high on both, reaching 92.6-98.3% valid-information availability with 98.4-99.5% invalid-information rejection on ManBench-Return, within 3.8 points of the best baseline's overall accuracy. On STALE Type II it improves Overall over the strongest comparison policy by 22.3 (Qwen), 18.5 (Gemini), and 27.5 (DeepSeek) points at roughly 2.3 times their tokens, while a write-time consolidation pipeline is more accurate still at 3.99 times TRACE's.
papers.llm_summary: TRACE quản lý tính hợp lệ của memory khi agent quay lại sau thay đổi shared state, dùng eligibility decision training-free thay vì storage/retrieval thông thường.
papers.llm_reason: Core agent memory với benchmark thật (Memora, STALE II); insight invalidation memory hữu ích cho agent dài hạn nhưng business/marketing/content ít liên quan.

papers.title: Discovering Efficient and Explainable Communication Topologies for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems via Causal Inference
papers.abstract: The performance of large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) largely depends on effective communication topologies. Existing topology generation methods, however, typically learn communication topologies through black-box optimization driven solely by task-level rewards. While effective, such optimization provides little insight into why particular communication edges are selected, making it difficult to identify the critical communication subgraphs responsible for successful collaboration. To address this limitation, we propose E2-Explainer, a model-agnostic framework for providing interpretable explanations of communication topologies produced by arbitrary topology generators. Specifically, we formulate topology explanation as a causal attribution problem that identifies compact communication subgraphs supported by edge-level evidence of task preservation. We obtain this evidence with a Granger-style objective that measures how masking each communication channel changes the task outcome and the stability of the final response. The resulting budgeted subgraphs are then distilled into an amortized explainer, enabling efficient post-hoc explanation without repeated edge-level evaluations at deployment. Extensive experiments on multiple reasoning and coding benchmarks demonstrate that E2-Explainer identifies critical communication subgraphs that preserve successful collaboration. These subgraphs can also be executed directly to prune redundant communication edges, substantially reducing communication costs while maintaining competitive task performance.
papers.llm_summary: E2-Explainer dùng causal inference để giải thích white-box topology giao tiếp nào trong MAS thực sự quyết định thành công.
papers.llm_reason: Relevant MAS, benchmark reasoning/coding thật, insight 'subgraph then chốt' hữu ích khi thiết kế workflow agent nhưng hơi nghiên cứu.

papers.title: Harness-RL: Black-Box Reinforcement Learning with Action-Args Decoupling for Central-Agent Multi-Agent Harnesses
papers.abstract: Large language model agents increasingly solve long-horizon tasks through multi-agent harnesses in which a central agent coordinates specialized sub-agents, tools, and environments. Training the central policy in such a harness raises two challenges. First, an action label is a low-cardinality decision, whereas its args form a high-dimensional conditional sequence; optimizing both with a shared sequence-level signal can produce conflicting gradients. Second, dynamic scheduling creates interdependent sessions with branches, parallel calls, and rewritten contexts, which cannot be faithfully reduced to one flat token sequence. We introduce Harness-RL, a structured reinforcement learning framework that combines Conflict-Aware Policy Optimization (CAPO) with interface-level black-box trajectory construction. The black-box component captures Interface Call Records, builds per-session prefix trees, and aligns outcome and process rewards with trainable tokens. CAPO uses forward activations to identify parameter partitions associated with action and args tokens, then routes their policy gradients to the corresponding subspaces. Harness-RL supports both central-only and joint multi-agent training. Across seven multi-hop question answering and agentic retrieval benchmarks, it reaches average F1 scores of 42.93 and 47.79 with Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen2.5-3B, respectively, while ablations validate the contribution of CAPO and favor central-only optimization in the evaluated setting. Our code is available at https://github.com/jiangxinke/Harness-RL.
papers.llm_summary: Harness-RL: RL black-box tách action/args và tree per-session để huấn luyện central agent trong harness multi-agent.
papers.llm_reason: Core multi-agent/RL mạnh với 7 benchmark và F1 rõ ràng, nhưng là phương pháp huấn luyện nặng, ít ứng dụng trực tiếp cho solopreneur content.

papers.title: DentAgent: Evidence-Centric Multi-Agent Coordination for Multimodal Dental Reasoning
papers.abstract: Oral diseases affect billions of people worldwide, underscoring a pressing need for accurate and reliable dental assessment that integrates heterogeneous evidence from domain knowledge, radiographs, intraoral photographs, and 3D dental data. Most existing dental AI systems remain modality- or task-specific. Although recent vision-language models support flexible dental question answering, directly generated response leaves evidence implicit and untraceable. To address these limitations, we introduce DentAgent, an evidence-centric multi-agent framework, in which the Orchestrator coordinate five specialized agents spanning various modalities. Each specialist utilizes domain tools to convert observations into structured evidence records. The Evidence Blackboard manages these records as a shared evidence state, tracking coverage, gaps, and conflicts before response generation. This standardized evidence representation integrates isolated dental capabilities into a unified agentic workflow. Across four benchmarks, DentAgent demonstrates leading performance, even surpassing the senior specialists by 17.3 percentage points on multi-label diagnosis, which supports its value for broadly applicable and traceable multimodal dental reasoning, and highlights its potential as a technical foundation for population oral health assessment and management.
papers.llm_summary: DentAgent: multi-agent evidence-centric với Orchestrator + 5 specialist + Evidence Blackboard cho reasoning nha khoa đa modal.
papers.llm_reason: Core multi-agent tốt, 4 benchmark thật (vượt specialist 17.3pp); pattern orchestrator/blackboard có thể học cho content pipeline, nhưng niche dental hạn chế relevance business.

papers.title: Topology-Conditioned Backdoors: Language Models That Insert Vulnerabilities When They Infer They Are in a Multi-Agent System
papers.abstract: A language model may behave safely in a single-agent evaluation yet produce vulnerable code when its context suggests that it is part of a multi-agent system. We study this failure mode by fine-tuning Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to condition code generation on deployment topology inferred from prompt-level provenance cues. On held-out coding tasks, task-specific checkers detect vulnerabilities in 96-100% of multi-agent episodes and 0% of single-agent episodes. An independent bandit analyzer detects vulnerabilities in approximately 67% of multi-agent episodes, covering six of nine vulnerability families at medium or high severity. Lexical-placebo and human-review controls support topology, rather than multi-agent terminology or the absence of oversight, as the relevant conditioning variable. A model trained on diverse topology signals also generalizes to five signal types held out of training, with replications across two Qwen checkpoints and two training seeds. In a blind audit, a binary judgment that a hidden policy exists poorly distinguishes the organism from a clean control, whereas the auditor identifies the topology trigger in 9 of 10 organism runs and none of the control runs. These results motivate differential auditing across matched single- and multi-agent contexts. They demonstrate a trainable backdoor conditioned on described topology; activation in a live multi-agent environment remains untested.
papers.llm_summary: Chứng minh backdoor trainable trong LLM chỉ kích hoạt khi model 'suy ra' nó đang ở hệ multi-agent, tạo code vulnerable 96-100% trong multi-agent và 0% single-agent.
papers.llm_reason: Experiment thật trên Qwen2.5-7B, insight actionable (audit differential single vs multi-agent) quan trọng cho ai dùng multi-agent, nhưng là security research, business relevance gián tiếp.

papers.title: Persistent LLM Orchestration of Heterogeneous Robot Teams via Partial Delegation to Multi-Agent Protocols
papers.abstract: Natural language specifications let non-expert users task robot teams, and large language models (LLMs) have recently proven effective at grounding such semantic specifications into plans for heterogeneous teams. Existing approaches assume missions that terminate and environments that, while unknown, do not change, but both assumptions fail in many emerging applications. For example, a disaster-response mission does not terminate, and its environment changes continuously as hazards spread and evacuees move. We identify three ways an LLM orchestrator breaks in this setting: its prompt grows without bound, its reasoning degrades as agents and targets accumulate, and it stops actively monitoring after covering the search space once. We build on the successful framework of grounded generative intelligence, and address each issue with a classical idea. A Markovian state summary, rebuilt from the semantic map at every invocation, replaces the growing interaction history. Partial delegation lets the orchestrator assign a subset of robots to an autonomous multi-agent protocol and reserve its reasoning for generating subtasks that require detailed parameters and careful ordering. Lastly, observation staleness, surfaced explicitly in the prompt, together with task-and event-triggered re-prompting, keeps the team vigilant. In a simulated urban search-and-rescue mission with spreading fire and moving evacuees, our framework rescues 98% of civilians versus 89% for the strongest baseline while using six times fewer tokens. Additional ablations isolate the contribution of each mechanism.
papers.llm_summary: Giải quyết orchestrator LLM bị hỏng trong sứ mệnh dài hạn bằng summary trạng thái Markov, partial delegation cho multi-agent protocol và re-prompting theo event, trong mô phỏng cứu hộ đô thị.
papers.llm_reason: Multi-agent orchestration cốt lõi (30), sim urban search-and-rescue thật nhưng không phải domain kinh doanh (17), robot xa content (6), insight về context growth & staleness áp dụng cho agent làm việc lâu dài (11).

papers.title: ClinAgent: A ReAct-Based Agent for Conversational Access to Clinical Trial Information
papers.abstract: Querying clinical trial registries remains a manual and error-prone process, requiring researchers to navigate large volumes of semi-structured data without support for natural language interaction or cross-source synthesis. To address this, we introduce ClinAgent, a conversational system based on agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) that enables clinicians and researchers to query clinical trial information in plain language and receive grounded, up-to-date responses across multi-turn interactions. The system centers on a Large Language Model (LLM) agent following the ReAct paradigm, which iteratively reasons over queries, selects among a set of integrated tools, and refines its actions based on intermediate outputs. These tools include a ClinicalTrials.gov search interface, a PubMed module, and a Python-based analyzer operating on a locally cached structured dataset of clinical trials. We evaluate the system using a three-phase framework assessing operational effectiveness, planning quality, tool-use efficiency, and expert qualitative judgments, comparing three LLM backends: Gemini 3.0 Flash and two variants of DeepSeek V3.2 (thinking and non-thinking). Results reveal complementary strengths, with DeepSeek (thinking mode) excelling in planning quality, while Gemini achieves the highest overall performance and strongest expert ratings. Overall, our findings highlight the potential of agentic AI systems to improve the accessibility and synthesis of clinical trial information, supporting more efficient and user-centered biomedical research workflows.
papers.llm_summary: Giới thiệu ClinAgent, hệ thống agent ReAct với RAG và nhiều tool (ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed, Python analyzer) cho phép truy vấn thông tin thử nghiệm lâm sàng bằng ngôn ngữ tự nhiên, so sánh hiệu năng Gemini 3.0 Flash và DeepSeek V3.2.
papers.llm_reason: Rất liên quan agent/tool-use/ReAct/RAG với benchmark thực tế và so sánh nhiều LLM, tuy domain lâm sàng nhưng pattern kiến trúc agent có giá trị tham khảo cho content về AI agent.

papers.title: DocTalk: Enhancing Medical Knowledge Retrieval via Fine-tuned Large Language Models with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Robust Clinical Decision Support
papers.abstract: Objective: The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) in healthcare has opened new possibilities for AI-assisted clinical decision-making; however, safe and effective deployment remains challenging because of hallucination and domain misalignment. This study introduces DocTalk, a doctor-assistive question-answering (QA) system designed to generate concise, chart-grounded responses from de-identified discharge summaries. Methods: We developed a high-fidelity data generation pipeline that produces 500 clinically relevant QA pairs through sentence-level decomposition, chain-of-thought-guided question formulation, and expert review. Six open-source LLMs, including three general-purpose and three biomedical models, were evaluated before and after parameter-efficient instruction tuning using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). The framework integrates prompt engineering, in-context learning, and medically aligned evaluation to support factual and interpretable responses. Results: On DocTalk-QA, instruction tuning produced consistent improvements across lexical, semantic, and clinical fidelity metrics. The best-performing tuned model, Llama-3-Med42-8B, achieved ROUGE-L = 0.40, BERTScore-F1 = 0.76, and UMLS-F1 = 0.49. To examine external generalization beyond the DocTalk-QA dataset, the two best-performing models, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Llama-3-Med42-8B, were evaluated on PubMedQA before and after instruction tuning. Accuracy improved from 0.931 to 0.977 for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and from 0.935 to 0.943 for Llama-3-Med42-8B. Conclusion: DocTalk was deployed as a secure web-based platform for interactive EHR querying. These findings suggest that clinically grounded instruction tuning can improve medical QA performance and support practical clinical decision support.
papers.llm_summary: DocTalk xây pipeline 500 cặp QA từ discharge summary và fine-tune LoRA 6 LLM open-source cho QA lâm sàng grounded chart.
papers.llm_reason: LLM+RAG+CoT chuẩn (24), experiment thật với LoRA và metric rõ ràng (18), y tế nên xa nội dung AI cho người 30+ (8), nhưng mẫu 'data pipeline + LoRA + đánh giá' làm niche assistant được (13).

papers.title: LeafSkill: Efficient Leaf-Level Action Grounding for Recursive LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Recursive large language model (LLM) agents solve long-horizon tasks through decomposition, execution, and environmental feedback. Yet after producing an atomic subtask, they often invoke the same large model again to translate a familiar instruction into an executable action. We observe that high-level planning is task-specific, whereas leaf-level action grounding recurs across tasks and can be checked against environment-admitted actions. We introduce LeafSkill, an external reuse layer that retrieves semantically related grounding experience, binds action templates to current objects and admissible actions, and uses a lightweight 1.7B selector to choose a bound action or defer the unchanged subtask to the original agent. Skills remain outside the model parameters, allowing a frozen selector to use post-training additions. Under lexical and syntactic paraphrases, exact matching retrieves none of the reference actions, while semantic retrieval preserves 96.0% and 97.0% candidate coverage; the frozen selector adopts 97.34% of unseen skill types. On an independent confirmation set of 200 Robotouille tasks, LeafSkill completes 137 tasks versus 121 for ReCAP (68.5% vs. 60.5%, exact McNemar p=.0259). On the 106 tasks completed by both, it reduces Qwen3.5-27B tokens by 14.42% and calls by 14.08%. A separate held-out repeat yields a consistent 9.0-point success gain and 18.98% token reduction. Reusable leaf grounding can thus improve task completion while reducing host-model inference without replacing high-level planning.
papers.llm_summary: Giới thiệu LeafSkill, lớp reuse bên ngoài giúp recursive LLM agent grounded hành động leaf-level mà không cần gọi lại model lớn, giảm 14.42% token và tăng 16.5% thành công trên Robotouille.
papers.llm_reason: Pattern tách planning khỏi leaf-level action grounding với skill reuse rất thực tiễn, experiment mạnh với statistical significance, tiết kiệm token là insight actionable cho ai đang build với LLM.

papers.title: LLM-Aided Design for Manufacturing: A Multi-Agent System for Intent-Preserving Redesign of CAD for Improved Manufacturability
papers.abstract: We introduce autonomous, intent-preserving Design for Manufacturing (DFM) redesign of CAD parts: given an engineer's CAD model, the method returns a variant that is easier to manufacture without losing its design intent. Generating such a redesign in a single shot is unreliable, since CAD fidelity degrades as parts grow complex; we instead produce it as a sequence of individually verified design transitions. Our DFM-Redesign pipeline realizes this with two coupled agent subsystems driven by a pretrained multimodal LLM: a DFM Reviewer that inspects the current design and proposes one intent-preserving manufacturability improvement at a time, and a CAD Modifier that executes each proposal as an edit to the part's CadQuery program. The CAD Modifier closes a verification loop, compiling every candidate edit and visually checking it against the intended change from multi-view renderings, then re-generating or re-instructing until the edit is accepted or abandoned. Iterating review and verified modification compounds edits into parts more complex than one-shot generators reliably produce, preserves the original intent at each step, and requires no fine-tuning. On a 46-part benchmark scored by chamfer distance to reference geometries, the CAD Modifier reproduces target parts more accurately on average than chain-of-thought single agents given the same tools, and ablations isolate the contributions of the visual review loop and of captioning the design state before each edit. A centrifugal pump casing built from 32 chained transitions illustrates the complexity reachable by compounding verified edits. This is a preliminary report: evaluation of the full review-and-redesign loop, including manufacturability gain and an operational measure of intent preservation, is ongoing.
papers.llm_summary: Multi-agent multimodal LLM redesign CAD để dễ sản xuất mà giữ intent thiết kế, qua loop review+verify.
papers.llm_reason: Cấu trúc agent (reviewer+modifier+verify loop) hay và benchmark 46 chi tiết thật, nhưng niche CAD/sản xuất gần như không chạm content/business của bạn.

papers.title: DeepGroundRepair: From API-Grounded Generation to Shape-Aware Repair for Deep Learning Programs
papers.abstract: Deep learning programs are fundamental to modern AI applications, and automatically generating them from natural language requirements can substantially reduce DL development effort. Large language models have demonstrated promising capabilities for this direction. However, generated DL programs often remain unreliable because they must satisfy domain specific API usage constraints and tensor shape dependencies, violations of which can cause API level syntactic issues and runtime failures. Existing retrieval augmented generation and feedback guided code repair methods do not adequately address these DL specific constraints. In this paper, we propose DeepGroundRepair, a three stage framework that establishes a generation localization repair workflow to improve the reliability of LLM-generated DL programs. Its key idea is to progressively narrow the generation and repair spaces using DL specific knowledge and runtime tensor information. Specifically, it grounds generation in task-relevant API knowledge, localizes the upstream causes of tensor shape mismatch failures, and uses runtime tensor shapes to guide parameter repair. We evaluate DeepGroundRepair on the 100 model-level DL programming tasks in DeepEval using six open-weight LLMs across TensorFlow, PyTorch, and PaddlePaddle. We compare it with four baselines: two generation-only methods and their counterparts incorporating traceback guided self debugging. The results show that, relative to these baselines, DeepGroundRepair reduces the combined number of API-level syntactic issues by an average of 5.4 per 10 program files and achieves an average relative improvement of 85.3% in code executability. Compared with the two self debugging baselines, it improves semantic consistency by an average of 18.1% and reduces token cost by an average of 28.4%.
papers.llm_summary: Framework 3 giai đoạn ground API, localize lỗi shape tensor và repair code DL bằng LLM trên DeepEval với 6 model, 3 framework.
papers.llm_reason: AI/code core tốt, experiment thật, nhưng chỉ dành cho dev DL, ít liên quan content/marketing nên điểm trung bình.

papers.title: Semantic Candidate-Job Matching: A Comparative Evaluation of Dense Embedding Models in Hybrid Retrieval
papers.abstract: This paper presents a comparative evaluation of dense embedding models for semantic candidate-job matching in high-volume staffing workflows. Incoming job descriptions are converted into structured English search text and language-specific keywords through LLM-based parsing, and candidate profiles are indexed as semantically enriched resume representations. We evaluate EmbeddingGemma (base) against EmbeddingGemma fine-tuned with Cached Multiple Negatives Ranking Loss (MNRL) within a unified hybrid retrieval pipeline that fuses vector similarity and full-text relevance via reciprocal rank fusion (RRF), and benchmark both against the MPNet model on a batch comparative evaluation dataset scored through the deployed job-candidate matching scoring pipeline. We further document, with mathematical detail, the broader set of contrastive fine-tuning objectives considered during model development (including AnglE/CoSENT-style refinement) and the empirical rationale for retaining Cached-MNRL-only adaptation as the preferred configuration. To support reproducible model selection, we define a broader evaluation framework comprising standard information retrieval metrics (Recall@K, mean reciprocal rank, nDCG) under the exact hybrid-retrieval protocol; the metrics used for the evaluation reported in this paper are fine-tuning convergence diagnostics and a batch comparative evaluation using the deployed AI-Match score and an independent LLM-as-a-Judge relevance score, and we state this scope explicitly rather than implying the full framework was measured. The paper addresses the gap between general-purpose embedding benchmarks and enterprise job-candidate matching constraints, providing a structured basis for comparing embedding strategies under realistic job-candidate retrieval conditions.
papers.llm_summary: So sánh EmbeddingGemma base/fine-tune Cached-MNRL với MPNet trong hybrid retrieval match CV-việc làm bằng RRF.
papers.llm_reason: Benchmark embedding retrieval thật có Recall@k/MRR/nDCG, nhưng nghiệp tuyển dụng; framework chọn model vẫn áp dụng được cho search trong kênh content.

papers.title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models
papers.abstract: Many machine learning approaches are two-level: an expert selects a class of methods, within this class the choice of key components is critical and usually manual. This paper addresses the automatic tuning of these components and proposes a framework transferable across models of different nature. The multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework has three roles---analyst, coder, and recorder~---with an experiment log and a sandboxed execution environment. Unlike systems that optimize the entire ML script or search architectures in a discrete space, the framework operates over an open but semantically narrow space: the agent generates code only for the specified components, leaving the overall network structure unchanged. The approach is validated in two directions: tuning a classification spiking neural network with correlation learning, and solving high-order differential equations with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN). Across five tasks---spiking classification on MNIST and Digits, and boundary-value problems for the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky (KS) equations---the agent outperforms the baselines: classification accuracy is 13 percentage points (MNIST) and 6 percentage points (Digits) higher; the error against the analytical single-soliton solution is reduced approximately 2491-fold; the invariant-preservation error drops approximately 325-fold in the selected GNLSE run with a Gaussian perturbation and by more than 100-fold on average over repeated initializations; and the mass drift drops 14-fold for the KS problem with a Gaussian perturbation. The framework thus tunes key components on tasks of different nature without changing its internal structure.
papers.llm_summary: Hệ multi-agent LLM (analyst/coder/recorder) tự tune component NN chuyên biệt trong sandbox, thắng baseline trên 5 task.
papers.llm_reason: Experiment thật trên SNN/PINN nhưng kết quả thiên kỹ thuật ML; ý tưởng agent loop tune ít liên quan trực tiếp đến content/business ai.

papers.title: Beyond Independent Values: Optimal Auctions with Correlated Valuations for LLM-Native Advertising
papers.abstract: Conversational assistants are becoming the place where people ask what to buy, and sponsored content is moving into their answers. Several advertisers then compete for one sponsored slot, and all of them read the same conversation, so their willingness to pay usually moves together. Existing auctions for LLM advertising treat these values as independent. We therefore present AffMyerson, an auction that captures this correlation and turns it into revenue. We model the advertisers' values given the conversation as a multivariate normal and turn the economic premise of positive dependence (affiliation) into a sign condition on the precision matrix. We design a neural parameterization whose every output satisfies it. We prove that every prior in this family yields a truthful, ex-post individually rational auction, so estimation error can cost revenue but never truthfulness. We derive the conditional virtual values in closed form. By the design of the prior, pricing an auction needs no matrix inversion and takes O(n^2) time, fast enough to run at query time. We also work out the log-normal family used in empirical ad-auction work. There we prove that the auction is truthful for every prior and revenue-optimal when the prior is correct, and that the virtual value is regular everywhere whenever the conditional spread is below a loose threshold, which our fitted priors stay well under. With LLM-agent bidders, AffMyerson earns 6.2% more than a second-price auction with a tuned reserve, 6.1% more than Ronen's lookahead auction with the same prior, and 9.2% more than Myerson's auction run as if values were independent. This gain is still 4.5% on real keyword search queries where willingness to pay is hard to read. The correlation comes from common demand. Agents that judge the conversation bid together and agents told to calculate do not. The gain from conditioning moves with the correlation.
papers.llm_summary: AffMyerson thiết kế auction tối ưu cho quảng cáo trong trợ lý hội thoại khi giá trị nhà quảng cáo tương quan dương, truthful và pricing chỉ O(n²).
papers.llm_reason: Cực kỳ relevant business AI (monetize LLM answers, sponsored content) nhưng thiên lý thuyết kinh tế-hóa, ít benchmark thực nghiệm và khó hành động trực tiếp cho solopreneur nhỏ.

papers.title: Kolibri: A Sovereign European Model on the Pareto Frontier
papers.abstract: This report introduces Kolibri, an English-German mixture-of-experts transformer with 78.1B total parameters and 3.46B active parameters per token, released as open weights under the Apache 2.0 licence. We built Kolibri for sovereign and specialised deployment, with a particular focus on German and on regulated domains such as public administration, industry, and aerospace. To support these settings, we control the full model-development process, including data, architecture, training infrastructure, post-training, and evaluation. We train Kolibri on 24T tokens across pre-training, mid-training, and long-context extension, with German accounting for more than 20% of the data mix by bytes. To reach this share, we complement German datasets with more than 2T German tokens that we curate from the web with our own pipeline and generate synthetically. Post-training combines supervised fine-tuning on curated German and English data with reinforcement learning on more than 1.2M internally curated tasks, which cover reasoning, tool use, instruction following, code, and retrieval. The model activates 4.4% of its parameters per token, and among the open models evaluated in this report, it lies on the Pareto frontier of quality and serving cost in English and German. Kolibri builds on Kolibri Origin, an earlier iteration that validated our full pipeline at scale. Both models come from our Model Factory, which connects data, experimentation, training, evaluation, and deployment through version-controlled workflows.
papers.llm_summary: Kolibri là model MoE 78B tham số (3.46B active) open-weight Apache 2.0, huấn luyện 24T tokens chuyên cho tiếng Đức-Anh, nằm trên Pareto frontier chất lượng/chi phí trong các model open-source.
papers.llm_reason: Model open-source đáng chú ý với pipeline full-stack minh bạch, nhưng focus tiếng Đức/châu Âu nên ít liên quan trực tiếp đến content/business AI tiếng Việt của solopreneur.

papers.title: Read the Route: Attention-Steered Hypergraph Retrieval for Multi-hop RAG
papers.abstract: Graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG) answers multi-hop questions by organizing a corpus into a graph and retrieving along its structure. Existing retrieval methods face two limitations. Diffusion- and similarity-based methods expand retrieval along fixed edge weights or by similarity to the question, without resolving its implicit entity references, allowing relevance errors to accumulate across hops. In contrast, exploration-based methods let an LLM reason about the next hop, but require a separate generation at each hop, leading to high inference costs. We observe that an LLM can resolve implicit entity references from retrieved passages and a multi-hop question before generating any tokens. Further analysis identifies a small set of attention heads, termed addressing heads, that capture this capability across multiple hops in a single forward pass. Building on this finding, we propose HyperAddress, which runs Personalized PageRank on a description-labelled hypergraph, using addressing heads to determine the restart distribution and transition weights, thereby guiding multi-hop retrieval without any generation at query time. On MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and HotpotQA, HyperAddress outperforms the strongest baseline by 3.5 points of Recall@5 and 7.4 points of All@5 on average, with gains that grow with the number of hops. It answers more than twice as fast and builds its index at half the cost.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất HyperAddress dùng attention heads để hướng dẫn retrieval đa bước trên hypergraph trong GraphRAG, không cần sinh token lúc query, đạt hiệu năng và tốc độ tốt hơn baseline trên các benchmark multi-hop QA.
papers.llm_reason: RAG và retrieval là chủ đề AI cốt lõi, có benchmark rõ ràng, nhưng quá kỹ thuật hạ tầng, ít liên quan trực tiếp content/business và insight hành động cho solopreneur hạn chế.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Causality Assessment (MARCA) of Individual Case Safety Reports in Pharmacovigilance
papers.abstract: Introduction: Increasing volumes of individual case safety reports (ICSRs) challenge expert-led causality assessment in pharmacovigilance. We developed MARCA (Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Causality Assessment), a four-agent framework for Naranjo-based assessment, and evaluated agreement with human experts and exploratory differences between non-RAG and RAG-labelled scores. Methods: MARCA combined scientific literature retrieval, drug-label assessment, objective-evidence classification, and clinical causality reasoning using Gemini 2.5 Pro and DeepSeek-V3.2. Agent-generated rationales informed human-assisted scoring. A consensus expert reference standard covered 215 ICSRs and 1,562 drug-event combinations (DECs) from FAERS (Q1-Q2 2025). Agreement was measured using percentage agreement and Cohen's kappa. Results: Question-level agreement was 96.8% for Naranjo Q2 (kappa = 0.491; 95% CI 0.265-0.663), 85.4% for Q5 (kappa = 0.269; 95% CI 0.180-0.340), and 96.8% for Q10 (kappa = 0.922; 95% CI 0.885-0.951). Final causality classification agreement was 79.4% (95% CI 71.8-85.3; kappa = 0.587, 95% CI 0.450-0.690). In a retrospective subset of 60 DECs, agreement was higher for RAG-labelled than non-RAG scores for Q5 (83.3% vs 65.0%) and Q10 (100.0% vs 18.3%). Discussion: MARCA-assisted assessment showed substantial variation in agreement across Naranjo questions, with lower concordance for alternative causes. Retrospective RAG comparisons are exploratory and do not establish prospective effectiveness.
papers.llm_summary: MARCA là framework 4 agent RAG đánh giá nhân-quả Naranjo cho báo cáo an toàn thuốc, so agreement với chuyên gia trên 215 ICSR từ FAERS.

papers.title: HakiCC: LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Design and Optimization of Concurrency Control Protocols
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have recently been applied in systems research as a tool to reduce human-intensive engineering effort through cost-efficient automation. Decades of research have produced a rich landscape of concurrency control (CC) protocols, each encoding distinct trade-offs in correctness, throughput, and abort behavior. However, most applications in practice default to 2PL or OCC, because selecting and adapting a protocol to a specific application requires expert knowledge that is rarely available to application designers. This is a wasted opportunity, as an application-specific CC protocol can yield significant performance advantages over a generic baseline, but designing one requires deep expertise in CC protocol design. In this paper, we propose HakiCC, an LLM-driven multi-agent pipeline that automatically designs, verifies, and optimizes concurrency control protocols tailored to a given target application. HakiCC provides a two-stage pipeline. In Stage 1, a multi-agent system takes a workload description as input and generates an application-specific CC protocol implementation, which is iteratively repaired and verified for conflict-serializability. In Stage 2, the verified protocol is further optimized for that application through an LLM-driven evolutionary loop targeting correctness and throughput. We evaluate HakiCC on TPC-C and AuctionMark as target workloads, producing and reporting ten application-specific CC protocols. All ten are conflict-serializable after Stage 1; Stage 2 improves throughput for every protocol, with average gains of +50.6% for TPC-C protocols and +92.2% for AuctionMark protocols.
papers.llm_summary: HakiCC dùng multi-agent LLM tự thiết kế, verify và tối ưu protocol concurrency control cho từng ứng dụng.
papers.llm_reason: Multi-agent LLM có thật trên TPC-C/AuctionMark nhưng lĩnh vực database chuyên sâu, ít giá trị ứng dụng cho solopreneur content/business.

papers.title: MIRROR: Multipath Quorum Integrity for LLM Multi-Agent Communication
papers.abstract: Inter-agent communication is central to Large Language Model Multi-Agent Systems (LLM-MAS), but it introduces an underexplored vulnerability: Agent-in-the-Middle (AiTM) attacks that manipulate messages in transit without compromising the agents themselves. Prior work reports Attack Success Rates (ASR) approaching 100% on structured tasks. Existing defenses rely on semantic validation, which requires additional inference and can block benign outputs, or on transport-layer encryption, which does not help when an intermediary legitimately terminates TLS. We present MIRROR, a communication-layer integrity primitive that replicates a single canonicalized payload across k logical routes and accepts a message only when a strict majority of routes report the same digest. MIRROR uses unkeyed hashing and so authenticates nothing on its own, since an active on-path adversary can always recompute a digest over a payload it has modified. All integrity derives from the assumption that honest routes form a majority. The digest serves only to make witness routes constant-size and to bind the recovered payload to the quorum-agreed value under second-preimage resistance. We give the guarantee under a route-compromise bound alpha < 0.5, and extend it to correlated routes, where the quantity that matters is the size of the largest shared-failure group and not the route count. We further show that availability and integrity degrade at the same threshold: below alpha = 0.5, quorum-denial and message-dropping adversaries cannot block honest traffic. Across MMLU, HumanEval, and MBPP on two frameworks and four communication topologies, and in a MetaGPT deployment against a production API, MIRROR reduces ASR to 0% below the threshold at 1x LLM token cost. LLM-as-a-Judge costs 35x in the same deployment, and blocks up to 44.2% of benign outputs in the topology sweep.
papers.llm_summary: MIRROR phòng tấn công Agent-in-the-Middle bằng cách nhân bản payload qua k route và chỉ chấp nhận khi đa số route cùng digest, dưới giả thiết honest route chiếm đa số.
papers.llm_reason: Multi-agent communication cốt lõi (28), defense có phân tích guarantee nhưng benchmark thực tế hạn chế (15), xa business/content (5), insight quorum integrity thiên hạ tầng, ít dùng trực tiếp (13).

papers.title: Reasoning Quality Matters: Combating Reasoning Collapse in LLM-based Embedding Learning
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently shown strong potential for producing context-rich text embeddings for retrieval. Most existing methods either treat embedding learning as passive feature extraction or exploit LLM reasoning through instruction following for better embedding optimization. However, specialization toward embedding objectives can suppress useful reasoning generation or produce retrieval-irrelevant text. We refer to these two forms of degradation as reasoning collapse. To address this issue, we propose CoFree (Collapse-Free Reasoning Embedding), a two-stage framework that progressively integrates LLM reasoning into query and document embedding optimization while preserving reasoning quality. At the first stage, CoFree applies reference-guided supervised fine-tuning to restore the reasoning ability and retain representational strength of the foundation embedding model. At the second stage, we introduce dual rewards, an embedding-oriented reward and a reasoning-oriented reward, to guarantee fine-grained reasoning of the relevance toward the embedding goal in reinforcement learning. This endpoint-coupled optimization transforms embedding learning from static alignment into a high-quality reasoning-guided search process for retrieval. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of CoFree, with CoFree-4B achieving an average absolute improvement of 2.8 nDCG@10 points over Qwen3-Embedding-4B across 22 datasets from MTEB and BRIGHT. Online experiments in a real-world retrieval system further show consistent gains. Code, RTED, and model checkpoints will be made publicly available.
papers.llm_summary: CoFree là framework hai giai đoạn ngăn reasoning collapse khi dùng LLM tạo embedding cho retrieval, kết hợp reference-guided SFT và dual reward RL (embedding + reasoning) để cải thiện chất lượng truy xuất.
papers.llm_reason: Kỹ thuật embedding/retrieval quan trọng và có experiment rõ ràng nhưng quá kỹ thuật, insight gián tiếp, ít actionable cho solopreneur content/business AI.

papers.title: Agentic AI Orchestration Framework for Spatial Intelligence: Supply Chain Deployment
papers.abstract: Industrial spatial decisions are assembled across systems that share neither a reference frame nor an owner, and analysts spend substantial effort reconciling those systems rather than reasoning about space. This paper presents ANASSA, a reference architecture integrating structured reasoning, multi-agent workflow orchestration, authoritative spatial grounding, and feedback-driven execution, and reports its instantiation in an operating supply-chain deployment. The architecture places typed data contracts at agent boundaries, validates spatial claims against a certified authoritative foundation, and enforces two blocking human-in-the-loop approvals inside a six-step cognitive loop. The deployment covers multi-hazard risk assessment on an ocean-and-inland freight lane, including cold-chain excursion detection over container telemetry. Across a three-month proof of concept (POC) with three implementation iterations, three deployment outcomes are reported: 25% improvement in data quality, 50% reduction in spatial workflow runtime, and 60% lower decision latency relative to the preceding manual workflow. Absolute deployment-scale quantities and baseline counts are confidential; reported percentages are observed relative changes. These are uncontrolled deployment observations, not controlled experiments. We therefore specify instrumentation and ablation protocols for mechanism-level evaluation.
papers.llm_summary: Triển khai ANASSA, kiến trúc multi-agent orchestration cho spatial intelligence trong supply chain, cho thấy cải thiện 25% chất lượng dữ liệu, giảm 50% runtime và 60% latency quyết định sau 3 tháng POC thực tế.

papers.title: Evidence, Logic, and Compliance: Multi-Agent Structured Graph Reasoning with Expert Arbitration for Medical Referral
papers.abstract: Medical referral (directing patients to the appropriate hospital department) is a complex decision-making process requiring the synthesis of multimodal data, including patient narratives, laboratory indicators, and radiology imaging. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have advanced medical dialogue systems, they struggle with real-world referral tasks due to two primary limitations: (1) Information Overload, where models fixate on high-frequency disease terms while overlooking subtle but critical urgency indicators; and (2) Unstructured Collaboration, where existing multi-agent frameworks rely on loose dialogue that leads to semantic drift and confirmation bias. To address these challenges, we introduce MASGR (Multi-Agent Structured Graph Reasoning), a framework that treats referral not as a classification task but as a structured graph construction problem. MASGR deploys specialized agents to extract evidence from distinct modalities and coordinates them through a clinical reasoning graph. This graph forces agents to establish explicit logical connections between conflicting evidence. Furthermore, we integrate a knowledge-guided arbitration mechanism that prioritizes patient safety rules over standard diagnostic classification. Extensive experiments on real-world medical records demonstrate that MASGR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art LLMs and existing multi-agent systems, particularly in complex cases requiring the balancing of chronic disease management and emergency intervention. The AI contribution lies in the Multi-Agent Structured Graph Reasoning framework that transforms unstructured multi-agent dialogue into a verifiable logical graph construction. The engineering application is demonstrated through its deployment in a complex healthcare decision-making system to optimize the precision of complex medical referrals.
papers.llm_summary: MASGR dùng multi-agent reasoning trên đồ thị có trọng tài chuyên gia để làm medical referral, vượt SOTA trên hồ sơ y khoa thật bằng cách ép kết nối logic giữa bằng chứng xung đột.

papers.title: CoEvoke: Evoking Multi-Agent Collaboration for Trajectory Collection
papers.abstract: Training multi-agent collaboration requires trajectories of checking, feedback, and repair, yet task-solving rollouts may end in immediate approval or repeat unsuccessful attempts without useful correction. We introduce CoEvoke, a cross-domain framework that evokes these interactions during trajectory collection. Controlled perturbations create recoverable difficulties, while restricted reference-based guidance directs investigation. The resulting dataset contains 4,567 reconstructable trajectories over 4,130 software-engineering and reasoning tasks, linking public interactions to evidence, decisions, and task-native outcomes. Separate experiments over 2,287 same-task pairs show feedback increases of 47.72-100 percentage points across seven perturbation groups; guidance has smaller, model-dependent effects. With identical training tasks, decision-record counts, and updates, perturbation-enriched judge training improves ACPBench-Hard success from 35.38% to 42.12% (+6.73 points). SWE verifier training gains 7.60-9.40 points over interface-matched untrained references. Workflow and post-training evaluations preserve task-solving topology with unperturbed inputs and no private-reference guidance. These results support designing collection conditions to obtain corrective supervision that improves collaborative decisions with frozen solving agents.
papers.llm_summary: CoEvoke tạo nhiễu có kiểm soát khi thu thập trajectory để mô hình multi-agent học check-feedback-repair, cải thiện ACPBench-Hard và SWE verifier.

papers.title: LLM-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive NPC Behavior in Multi-Agent Combat Games
papers.abstract: Scripted and rule-based non-player characters (NPCs) in combat video games often exhibit predictable behaviors that experienced players can exploit, while reinforcement learning (RL) agents typically retain a fixed policy after training and cannot readily adapt their strategy to different opponents. We investigate a runtime strategy-selection framework in which a large language model (LLM) guides a trained RL policy without modifying its underlying behavior. To demonstrate this, we train five NPC agents with a shared PPO policy in Unity and compare a baseline configuration, in which the policy acts independently, with an LLM-augmented configuration in which a locally hosted Mistral 7B model, accessed through Ollama, reads the live game state every five seconds and assigns one of four tactical tags. We evaluate both configurations against three scripted opponent types across 600 episodes and analyze outcomes using the Mann-Whitney U test. Against a Balanced opponent that changes tactics during an episode, the LLM-augmented agents more than doubled their win rate from 11% to 24% and produced significantly longer episodes. Against an Evasive opponent, the augmented agents achieved a higher win rate and faster kills, although their shorter episode duration did not satisfy the strict hypothesis definition. Against an Aggressive opponent, the LLM's near-constant preference for encirclement was counterproductive. Analysis of 2,430 strategy selections showed that Surround was selected in 83.8% of cases regardless of opponent type, indicating limited zero-shot strategic differentiation at this model scale. These results demonstrate both the potential and limitations of LLM-guided runtime strategy selection for adaptive multi-agent game AI.
papers.llm_summary: Dùng LLM local (Mistral 7B qua Ollama) gán tag chiến thuật runtime để điều khiển NPC PPO trong Unity combat, 600 episodes, test Mann-Whitney, win-rate vs Balanced tăng 11→24%.
papers.llm_reason: LLM+RL agent cho game có liên quan AI (22), experiment Unity/Ollama/600 episodes có thống kê thật (19), góc game AI có thể làm content nhưng hẹp (8), pattern strategy-tag runtime áp dụng được giới hạn (10).

papers.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: A vulnerability costs more to fix the later it is discovered. As coding agents generate code faster than developers can review it, software needs a first line of defense screening each new function in real time. LLM agents have recently become capable of finding real-world vulnerabilities by working as a security expert would: they run analysis tools, explore the surrounding code, test hypotheses and weigh the evidence before forming their own judgement. This reasoning, however, spans many model calls, so that each verdict takes minutes of compute, far too long for real-time screening. Faster detectors, which fine-tune deep learning models or prompt an LLM for a direct verdict, are less accurate: they judge a function without the context an agent gathers, and an LLM's generated verdict is unreliable even when given some of it. We present REVA (REal-time Vulnerability Analysis), an AI vulnerability detector that brings the security context and code understanding components behind agentic detectors into a single forward pass of an LLM. For each new function, REVA gives the LLM a pre-computed threat model of its module, lightweight static analysis findings and call-graph information. REVA leverages a trained probe to read the LLM's internal representations of the new function in this context. On PrimeVul's held-out test set, REVA on GLM-5.3-Flash reaches 60.0% accuracy in about one second per function. This matches VulTriage (59.2%), the state-of-the-art agentic detector, run on the same LLM, while being over 250 times faster and less than a tenth as costly. On the same prompt, the probe is 14% to 17% more accurate than the LLM's own direct verdict. Across three open LLMs, REVA is at least as accurate as VulTriage, and about 10% more accurate on two of them. An LLM's internal representations thus encode much of what agentic detectors obtain through reasoning.
papers.llm_summary: REVA phát hiện lỗ hổng bảo mật real-time bằng contextual probing trên LLM trong single forward pass, kết hợp pre-computed threat model, static analysis findings và call-graph, đạt 60% accuracy trên PrimeVul.
papers.llm_reason: AI bảo mật trending, có benchmark thật và speed impressive, nhưng ứng dụng trực tiếp vào content business của solopreneur còn hạn chế, chủ yếu là topic content tiềm năng.

papers.title: CoEvolve: Counterfactual-Guided Co-Evolution of Memory and Collaboration in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems have demonstrated remarkable capabilities across diverse tasks. Yet their memory and collaboration architectures often remain static, constraining continued adaptation and improvement over time. Recent work addresses this limitation by evolving memory or collaboration based on interaction experience. However, updates to these interdependent components are not necessarily aligned: an evolved workflow may require experience that memory does not provide, while evolved memory may encode guidance that the workflow cannot use. To address this problem, we propose CoEvolve, a skill-centered framework for aligned memory--collaboration evolution. CoEvolve represents reusable local collaboration patterns as skills that link evolving collaboration decisions to their supporting memories. It further compares original and counterfactual trajectories to identify local evolution signals, which coordinate updates to the skill library, skill memory, and executor memories across rounds. Experiments on the ALFWorld and WebShop benchmarks confirm that CoEvolve achieves the best overall performance among the evaluated baselines, while ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of aligned co-evolution and counterfactual-guided evolution.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất CoEvolve, framework cho phép memory và collaboration architecture của multi-agent LLM cùng tiến hóa dựa trên counterfactual trajectories, đạt SOTA trên ALFWorld và WebShop.
papers.llm_reason: Rất liên quan đến thiết kế multi-agent LLM với experiment tốt, nhưng insight hành động cho content creator/business solopreneur còn hạn chế vì thiên về kỹ thuật nghiên cứu.

papers.title: NDT Factory: Synthesizing Verified Network Digital Twins from Semantic Models via Multi-Agent LLM
papers.abstract: Autonomous network management requires systems that can evaluate Network Service Intents (NSIs) under varying conditions without manual implementation of analysis logic, as envisioned in TM Forum Level~4 (L4) autonomy. Behavioral Network Digital Twins (NDTs) enable such evaluation, but existing NDTs rely on pre-defined analytical logic, limiting adaptability for evolving closed-loop control. This paper introduces the NDT factory, a multi-agent software system that synthesizes executable behavioral NDTs on demand from semantic models using Large Language Model (LLM). We validate the system using a Call Admission Control (CAC) case study, where deterministic what-if analysis serves as the admission decision process. The NDT factory generates a complete CAC NDT through parallel synthesis and orchestration, achieving 100% compilation and test pass rates across multiple runs. Simulation over 300 NSIs shows 99.3% decision agreement with a reference implementation, 90% admission rate, and correct attribution of all rejections, demonstrating reliable synthesis with deterministic, verifiable execution.
papers.llm_summary: NDT Factory dùng multi-agent LLM tổng hợp Network Digital Twin có thể kiểm chứng từ semantic model, đạt 100% pass build/test và 99,3% đồng thuận quyết định trên 300 Network Service Intent.
papers.llm_reason: Multi-agent LLM nhưng domain telecom rất hẹp (24), kết quả xác minh tốt (18), không liên quan content/marketing (5), insight decomposition orchestration transferable thấp (12).

papers.title: DRILS: Dependency-based Requirement Change Impact Analysis Using LLMs
papers.abstract: Change is inevitable in software systems, where requirements must continuously adapt to evolving stakeholder needs, regulations, and project scopes. Managing such changes is a fundamental software engineering challenge, as manually identifying the impact of a change request, given high requirements volume, Natural Language (NL) complexity, and intricate interdependencies, is error-prone and time-consuming. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer promising solutions for requirements change impact analysis (CIA), yet their effectiveness when enhanced with advanced techniques remains underexplored. We present DRILS, an LLM-based agentic framework for requirements Change Impact Analysis, employing a multi-agent architecture to generate candidate impact sets, with an LLM-as-a-judge promoting diversity during selection. DRILS features two key components: RE-RAG, a carefully engineered RAG technique providing focused domain context, and a requirement dependency graph (RDG) as an additional knowledge source. Evaluation across three manually curated datasets demonstrates superior performance over state-of-the-art baselines, achieving an average recall of 87.1%, precision of 76.3%, and F1 score of 81% at a lower cost. Precision gains are particularly significant, 41.1%, 83.4%, and 149.8% over the closest baseline per dataset, as higher precision directly reduces false positives and manual validation effort. We also contribute three annotated CIA datasets to support future research.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất DRILS, framework multi-agent dùng LLM với RAG chuyên biệt (RE-RAG) và đồ thị phụ thuộc yêu cầu để phân tích tác động thay đổi yêu cầu phần mềm, đạt F1 81% trên 3 dataset.

papers.title: Who Are They to Each Other? Multi-Agent Reasoning for Speaker Relationship Inference
papers.abstract: Inferring speaker relationships from spoken conversations is an important step towards socially aware speech understanding. However, this task remains underexplored, and supervised modeling is costly to train and scale. At the same time, existing inference-time LLM approaches provide limited structure for handling subtle, distributed, and multimodal relational cues that may support multiple plausible interpretations. To address these limitations, we introduce a training-free multi-agent reasoning framework that organizes inference through structured interaction among LLM agents, allowing relationship judgments to be proposed, challenged, and adjudicated without task-specific training. We instantiate this framework with two complementary designs. We propose Multi-Role Multi-Agent Debate as a task-specific adaptation of standard multi-agent debate for speaker relationship inference, assigning agents complementary roles or social-theory-grounded perspectives rather than a single undifferentiated viewpoint. In contrast, we introduce Multi-Agent Compete, a competition-based protocol that compares agent judgments through pairwise adjudication, eliminates weaker candidates, and retains the most defensible one. We evaluate these methods on the Seamless Interaction dataset across different modality settings, covering both binary classification and fine-grained relationship-detail prediction. Results suggest that they improve over zero-shot and existing multi-agent baselines in most cases. Human evaluation further suggests that this task is challenging even for people. LLM methods can sometimes outperform human annotators in text-included settings but are less competitive in the audio setting. Together, these findings suggest that relationship inference benefits from structured inference-time interaction among agents, while acoustic cues are not yet fully captured by current models.
papers.llm_summary: Framework multi-agent reasoning training-free (Multi-Role Debate và Multi-Agent Compete) để suy luận quan hệ người nói từ hội thoại, đề xuất-thách thức-phán xét trên dataset Seamless Interaction.

papers.title: GeoForge: Non-Parametric Self-Evolving Agents for Earth-Observation Reasoning
papers.abstract: Earth observation (EO) agents construct scientifically valid tool workflows and ground their conclusions in current geospatial evidence. This is challenging because EO workflows are constrained by sensing semantics, product dependencies, spatial and temporal compatibility, and parameter requirements. Existing agents often search a broad operation space for each query, while recent self-evolving systems do not fully organize heterogeneous EO trajectories into reusable knowledge across different decision levels. To solve this problem, we present GeoForge, a training-free, self-evolving framework that transforms completed trajectories into a structured nonparametric execution state. GeoForge constrains the operation space according to the sensing context, then retrieves a task-conditioned prior from three complementary memories. Workflow Graph Memory captures global operation order, Action-Level Experiences provide local corrections, and the Adapted Skill Standard Operating Procedure preserves procedural and data constraints. The retrieved prior guides tool execution, while current observations remain the basis of the final answer. After each task, a safety-gated distillation process converts grounded trajectories into reusable execution knowledge for future retrieval. This execution, distillation, and reuse loop improves planning without updating the backbone LLM. Experiments on multiple geospatial benchmarks demonstrate that GeoForge consistently improves both task accuracy and tool-use trajectory quality across diverse LLM backbones, while substantially reducing tool-planning and reasoning errors for most LLMs.
