papers.title: Back to the Future: Regressing Readability Features from LLMs
papers.abstract: Code readability supports software understanding, review, and maintenance. As AI coding agents become more widely used, readable code helps both humans review agent-generated output and agents maintain code within limited context windows. Yet existing readability models do not consistently agree with human judgements across datasets. We introduce BTTF (Back To The Future), pairing linear regression with information-theoretic features. Rather than using language models as black-box judges, BTTF uses them as measurement instruments. It combines traditional code measurements, embedding-based semantic organisation, and causal-LM predictability to capture source structure, semantic coherence, and contextual surprise. We evaluate BTTF on five publicly available human-rated readability benchmarks and our manually annotated MBJP development set, totalling 1,100 samples. BTTF improves average Spearman correlation over the strongest baseline by up to 0.101. Across 13 controlled readability-reducing transformations on production code, it achieves response rates of 93.8% in Java and 87.6% in Python, outperforming Dorn by 14% and 19.2%. It performs best among local models and trails the strongest cloud-LLM response by 1.7% in Java and 5.1% in Python. The direct-LLM baselines require an average of 1,083 prompt tokens per evaluation while remaining opaque. BTTF combines state-of-the-art benchmark performance and strong transformation robustness with feature-granular interpretability: every feature coefficient matches its theoretical directional effect across all evaluated model configurations.
papers.llm_summary: BTTF dùng LLM như thiết bị đo (không phải judge black-box) kết hợp feature cổ điển để dự đoán readability code, nhẹ token và giải thích được.
papers.llm_reason: Experiment vững (5 benchmark, 1.100 mẫu, Java/Python) và insight 'dùng LLM làm measurement instrument' có thể dùng cho content về AI coding, nhưng chủ đề code readability hẹp với người làm content.

papers.title: Did the Problem Actually Get Harder? Testing LLMs on Paired P and NP-Complete Problems Hardened by Adversarial Multi-Agent Rewriting
papers.abstract: Many NP-complete (NPC) problems have a polynomial-time (P) twin that differs in a single structural detail, such as 3- versus 2-colouring a graph. A model that reasons rather than recalls should notice which side of this boundary a problem falls on, yet existing benchmarks either fix the wording of each task or ignore its complexity class, so they cannot separate the two. We introduce P2NPCBench, a benchmark of 12 problem families in which every NPC problem is paired with a P twin posed over the same surface. To remove the textbook cues that enable recall, we build it with AgentGAN, an adversarial multi-agent framework in which a generator rewrites each statement until a panel of frozen code models fails, while an executable validity gate keeps every rewrite answer- and class-preserving. The result is 2,114 hardened statements with hand-verified reference human solvers. Evaluating 12 proprietary and open-source models, we find that every model scores lower on NPC statements than on their P twins (35.4% vs. 63.8% pass@1), and that 95.1% of model-family pairs fail more often on the NPC side. A tenfold time limit raises NPC accuracy only from 28.5% to 31.9%, so failures stem from wrong or crashing programs rather than slow ones. Hardening also narrows the class gap from 24.8 to 14.6 points, showing that part of the apparent gap reflects familiarity with textbook phrasing rather than complexity class.
papers.llm_summary: Xây dựng benchmark P2NPCBench với 2114 bài toán P/NP-complete được hardening bằng adversarial multi-agent rewriting (AgentGAN), cho thấy mọi LLM đều yếu hơn đáng kể trên NPC (35.4% vs 63.8%).
papers.llm_reason: Có benchmark lớn, đánh giá 12 model, insight về giới hạn reasoning của LLM—có thể dùng làm nội dung discuss về năng lực thực sự của AI, nhưng không trực tiếp actionable cho business.

papers.title: CasePlay: Self-Play Reinforcement Learning from Case Reports for Medical Reasoning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a promising way to improve the clinical reasoning abilities of large language models (LLMs), but current pipelines often rely on expert-labeled questions or costly synthetic-data generation. Meanwhile, the medical literature offers a wealth of high-quality unlabeled documents, including clinical case reports that trace the full clinical course from initial presentation to final treatment decisions. We study whether document-grounded self-play can convert these reports into effective RL training signals. We identify two challenges that limit existing self-play methods in this setting: knowledge-point fixation}, where the proposer repeatedly asks about a narrow set of salient clues in a source report, and difficulty-quality mismatch, where appropriately difficult questions may still be poorly formed or shallow, limiting their value for reasoner training. To address these challenges, we propose CasePlay, a self-play framework with two key components: (a) a Knowledge-Conditioned Proposer, which anchors question generation to case-specific knowledge points so that questions draw on a broader range of evidence from the source report; and (b) a Rubric-Judge Reasoner, which augments answer-accuracy feedback with rubric-based quality feedback on clue integration, reasoning depth, and option quality, guiding the proposer toward reasoning-intensive questions that better support reasoner training. Extensive experiments across seven medically related benchmarks demonstrate that CasePlay outperforms existing self-play baselines and improves the SFT warm-start model by 3.1 points on average, highlighted by a 6.3-point gain on LiveClin. This approach offers an effective path toward continually improving medical reasoning ability through self-play RL.
papers.llm_summary: CasePlay dùng self-play RL trên các case report y khoa để tạo bộ câu hỏi đào tạo reasoning, khắc phục fixation và mismatch chất lượng-khó bằng Knowledge-Conditioned Proposer và Rubric-Judge.
papers.llm_reason: Là LLM/RL nhưng lĩnh vực y khoa hẹp (27), methodology tốt ít benchmark số rõ (16), gần như không liên quan content/business của solopreneur (5), transferable được ý tưởng rubric-judge sang sản xuất content (10).

papers.title: Defense-in-Depth at the Perception-Reasoning Interface of LLM-Centric Agentic UAV Swarms
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly support Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarm operations such as data collection scheduling, where the model reads structured sensor reports and decides which sensors to visit. An adversary who quietly manipulates those reports can redirect the swarm without modifying the model weights or the UAV. Defenses for this interface have been proposed architecturally but rarely implemented or evaluated. We implement and evaluate defense-in-depth at the perception-reasoning interface of LLM-Centric Agentic UAV Swarms. Five layers check the provenance of a report, whether its values are physically admissible, whether they agree with what swarm geometry and service history predict, whether the resulting schedule starves any sensor, and, when these fail, hand control to a deterministic scheduler that ignores the suspect input. We test each layer against an adversary strong enough to defeat the layer before it. For each of the three input-side layers, we derive in closed form how far a report can be distorted before that layer reacts, fixing each boundary from deployment parameters before any attack data is collected; across thirty matched simulation runs, predicted and measured boundaries agree. Separating attack detection from response is a well-established principle, and we quantify the cost of neglecting this distinction at the perception-reasoning interface. When the system rejects a report, it replaces it with the most recent accepted report. This prevents the adversary from controlling the UAV schedule, but it also increases cumulative cost by 79% and 74% for the two detectors, respectively, compared with the undefended system. The safety check does not detect any attacks, but it nevertheless reduces the attack-induced cost by 37.5%.
papers.llm_summary: Implement defense-in-depth 5 lớp tại giao diện cảm nhận-reasoning của swarm UAV dùng LLM, với biên giới tấn đạo dạng đóng được kiểm chứng trên 30 chạy mô phỏng.
papers.llm_reason: Core agent/security và experiment tốt; principle tách phát hiện-phản ứng và kiểm chứng provenance áp dụng được, nhưng bối cảnh UAV xa với content business thực tế.

papers.title: Enhancing Human Mobility Prediction with Spatially Aware LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Predicting a user's next POI is a task in human mobility modeling, yet LLM-based approaches focus on semantic reasoning from previous mobility records, while neglecting real-world spatial context. However, human mobility is inherently shaped by spatial cognition, including geographic distance and neighborhood context. This issue is further compounded by prior evidence that LLMs often struggle with spatial reasoning tasks, including distance estimation and geographically biased prediction. To address these limitations, we propose our framework, a multi-agent LLM framework that decomposes next-POI prediction into three stages: Firstly, a Pattern Extraction Agent that captures temporal and categorical mobility patterns from trajectory history; Secondly, a Spatial Reasoning Agent that structures candidate activity choices by combining behavioral preferences with real-world spatial constraints, including geographic distance, road network distance, and neighborhood affiliation; and Thirdly, a Decision Synthesis Agent that integrates behavioral patterns and spatial reasoning for final prediction. Experiments on the NYC benchmark dataset with two LLM backbones show improvements over baseline methods, with up to 493% Hit@1 improvement and 37% relative improvement in Hit@5. Ablations show that combining neighborhood affiliation with distance-based features generally outperforms distance-only settings, and that the Spatial Reasoning Agent plays a crucial role in final prediction by integrating behavioral preferences with real-world spatial constraints, especially for smaller models. Overall, the results highlight the importance of spatial reasoning in mobility prediction. Accurate next-POI prediction requires combining behavioral patterns with explicit real-world spatial constraints, and multi-agent decomposition provides an effective structure for organizing these forms of context.
papers.llm_summary: Framework multi-agent LLM phân tích dự đoán POI tiếp theo bằng cách tách thành Pattern Extraction Agent, Spatial Reasoning Agent và Decision Synthesis Agent, cải thiện tới 493% Hit@1 trên benchmark NYC.
papers.llm_reason: Kiến trúc multi-agent thú vị để làm content nhưng bài toán dự đoán di chuyển quá niche, ít liên quan trực tiếp đến business/content AI của solopreneur.

papers.title: FlowMAS: Learning Multi-Agent Workflow Topology via Information-guided Generative Flow Network
papers.abstract: Automated multi-agent systems offer clear advantages over manually designed ones in scalability and adaptability, but existing workflow topology methods still face important limitations. Search-based methods are often computationally expensive, textual-gradient-based methods rely on coarse-grained feedback, and existing generation-based methods are not well suited to discrete workflow topologies with complex dependencies. To address these limitations, we propose FlowMAS, a multi-agent workflow topology method based on Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets). FlowMAS models workflow generation as reward-guided flow over the topology space and introduces three components: a GFlowNet-based topology generation backbone, a curiosity-driven module for structure-aware exploration, and an information-guided optimization module for evaluating intermediate topologies. Concretely, the curiosity-driven module encourages exploration of structurally novel workflows, while the information-guided module measures both the information contribution and the communication efficiency of different operators to favor more informative and effective collaboration patterns. Experiments on six benchmark datasets with three LLM backbones show that FlowMAS consistently outperforms multiple baselines.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất FlowMAS dùng Generative Flow Networks để tự động sinh topology workflow multi-agent tối ưu, với module curiosity-driven exploration và information-guided optimization, vượt baseline trên 6 benchmark.
papers.llm_reason: Liên quan multi-agent workflow automation, có experiment thật trên nhiều benchmark, nhưng GFlowNets khá niche và khó chuyển thành insight hành động cho solopreneur content.

papers.title: Agentic neural architecture search for clinical prediction from electronic health records: Cross-hospital knowledge transfer and computational efficiency
papers.abstract: Transformer architectures for clinical prediction from electronic health records (EHRs) often require costly manual tuning and may vary across hospitals and tasks. We introduce ATHENA (Agentic Transfer across Hospitals for EHR Neural Architecture Search), a knowledge-guided agentic neural architecture search framework for Transformer-based EHR modeling. A weight-sharing supernet is pretrained once per hospital, allowing candidate architectures to inherit weights and be evaluated through fine-tuning rather than independent pretraining. A two-layer cross-hospital prior supplies high-performing source architecture examples and task-specific component preferences summarized by SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based meta-regression. These priors guide a multi-agent large language model search using target-hospital validation feedback. Across six clinical prediction tasks at one held-out OneFlorida+ site and one external MIMIC-IV site, ATHENA significantly outperforms all four baselines in 9 of 12 site-task evaluations under a strict equal-compute comparison. In a separate comparison using a common pretrained AutoFormer supernet to isolate search strategy performance, ATHENA ranks first in 9 of 12 evaluations at a maximum search budget of 30 candidate evaluations. It also shows more consistent architecture selection across repeated searches. ATHENA supports more efficient architecture selection for Transformer-based clinical prediction models.
papers.llm_summary: ATHENA dùng multi-agent LLM search với prior cross-hospital (SHAP meta-regression) và supernet chia trọng số để tự động tìm kiến trúc Transformer dự đoán lâm sàng từ EHR.
papers.llm_reason: Mẫu multi-agent NAS + transfer learning có benchmark thật (9/12 thắng), nhưng healthcare/EHR chuyên biệt; chỉ học được ý tưởng 'prior + feedback loop' chứ khó áp dụng trực tiếp.

papers.title: Then there is prompt injection, a malicious email, ...: The Wild Wide West of OpenClaw Agentic System Security
papers.abstract: AI-powered personal assistant frameworks such as OpenClaw combine LLM reasoning, persistent memory, tool invocation, local execution, and web-based workflows. These capabilities enable useful automation, but they also create security risks when untrusted inputs, model reasoning, tools, memory, and deployment configuration interact without explicit trust boundaries. This paper presents an empirical study of reported security concerns in OpenClaw using two complementary data sources: Reddit discussions and security-tagged GitHub issues. We analyze more than 25K Reddit posts from 13 OpenClaw-related subreddits and identify 162 security-relevant posts with 1,787 associated comments. We further collect 358 security-tagged GitHub issues and retain 180 issues describing concrete security concerns. Using qualitative analysis and evidence-grounded CWE mapping, we identify 521 CWE instances across 59 distinct weakness types, concentrated in access-control failures, sensitive-data exposure, injection, and unsafe execution. We also extract 543 practitioner mitigation suggestions and consolidate them into seven recurring strategies. To complement the empirical analysis, we present an evidence-grounded illustrative reconstruction of a representative sensitive-data exposure pathway using dummy secret values. Our findings show that OpenClaw security issues are not isolated implementation bugs; they reflect recurring trust-boundary failures across the agent execution pipeline. We discuss how these weaknesses map to both traditional software-security categories and agent-specific failure mechanisms, and derive implications for safer agentic systems, including explicit trust boundaries, least-privilege tool access, execution containment, runtime oversight, and defense-in-depth deployment.
papers.llm_summary: Nghiên cứu thực nghiệm về bảo mật hệ thống agent OpenClaw qua phân tích 25K bài Reddit và 358 GitHub issues, xác định 521 CWE instances thuộc 59 loại yếu yếu, đồng thời tổng hợp 543 gợi ý mitigation thành 7 chiến lược lặp lại.
papers.llm_reason: Bảo mật agent AI là topic content nóng, data thực nghiệm mạnh, 7 chiến lược mitigation actionable; tuy nhiên OpenClaw là framework niche nên mức liên quan business trực tiếp hạn chế.

papers.title: Multi-agent LLMs on the Cloud-Edge-IoT Continuum: A Systematic Mapping Study on Architectures, Deployment, and Evaluation
papers.abstract: LLM applications are increasingly built as systems of cooperating components rather than as single prompt-response pipelines. IoT applications add constraints of their own, because sensing, reasoning, control, and actuation are spread across devices, edge nodes, and cloud services to meet latency, privacy, and bandwidth requirements. How multi-agent LLM systems are organized and deployed across this cloud-edge-IoT continuum has not been mapped systematically. We therefore conducted a systematic mapping study. From 831 records retrieved up to March 2026, we selected 45 primary studies and classified each one by architecture family, deployment pattern, application domain, and evaluation practice. We also recorded how each system was evaluated and whether its code or data are public. Five architecture families recur in the corpus. Specialized agent teams run next to sensors, planners delegate subtasks to workers, and small local models cooperate with large cloud models. A fourth group federates model adaptation across devices, and a large fifth group builds the supporting infrastructure for offloading, communication, memory, and serving. Deployment relies on six recurring patterns, ranging from local-only execution to control loops gated by policy checks or human approval. Twenty-four of the 45 studies target IoT, industrial, smart-home, healthcare, vehicular, or robotics settings, and 29 evaluate on physical hardware, where open models below 8B parameters dominate. Based on the mapping, we list the reporting items needed to make future evaluations comparable, give deployment guidance for common IoT constraints, and identify open problems.
papers.llm_summary: Thực hiện systematic mapping study phân loại 45 nghiên cứu về kiến trúc, deployment pattern và evaluation practice của hệ thống multi-agent LLM trên continuum cloud-edge-IoT.
papers.llm_reason: Survey tổng quan rất tốt để làm content về kiến trúc multi-agent LLM, nhưng là mapping study không có experiment gốc, và bối cảnh IoT ít liên quan trực tiếp đến solopreneur content/business.

papers.title: AgenticTwin: An Agentic LLM Framework Integrated with Digital Twin for Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Digital twins are increasingly used to monitor and simulate the behavior of cyber-physical systems. Even with skilled operators, interpreting anomalies detected within digital twin pipelines is challenging, as the sheer complexity and volume of raw sensor data make thorough analysis difficult. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) offer promising capabilities for reasoning and explanation, yet their integration into digital twin-driven anomaly analysis remains underexplored. In this work, we propose AgenticTwin, an agentic framework that integrates LLM-driven reasoning with a digital twin-based anomaly detection pipeline. The framework grounds LLM-generated explanations in outputs from a digital twin-driven anomaly classifier and enables human operators to ask relevant natural-language questions about the system. Beyond the framework itself, we introduce a benchmark-oriented evaluation pipeline constructed over synthetic anomalies injected into a real-world weather sensor dataset, enabling controlled generation of operator queries over anomaly events. We further evaluate the feasibility of deploying lightweight, open-source LLMs for practical cyber-physical environments. Experimental results demonstrate that structured agent collaboration and knowledge-grounded reasoning improve diagnosis quality, contextual retrieval, and mitigation quality across diverse possible anomaly scenarios.
papers.llm_summary: AgenticTwin kết hợp LLM agent reasoning với digital twin để phân tích anomaly, có benchmark pipeline trên dataset cảm biến thời tiết thật và evaluate LLM nhẹ.
papers.llm_reason: Core agentic framework với experiment thật nhưng niche cyber-physical; pattern grounding giải thích LLM vào đầu ra classifier hữu ích ở mức vừa phải cho solopreneur.

papers.title: Autonomous intelligence for mining productivity: a multi-agent AI approach to operational value creation
papers.abstract: Integrated Remote Operation Centres (IROCs) are emerging as the architectural frontier of Industry 4.0 for capital-intensive sectors such as mining, oil and gas, and energy. Yet two intertwined gaps constrain their evolution towards full autonomy. First, no integrated agentic architecture has been proposed for mining IROCs that orchestrates Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition systems, digital twins, predictive analytics and human-machine interfaces under safety-critical constraints. Second, no evaluation framework jointly addresses the real-time, Health-Safety-Environment, regulatory-auditability and cost-per-decision requirements that govern industrial agentic deployments. This paper makes four contributions. It synthesises industry needs and quantified gains documented in analogous industries that motivate an agentic approach to mining IROCs. It introduces EI2ROC, a three-tier multi-agent architecture combining a Large Language Model orchestrator with specialised monitoring and production-capacityprediction agents communicating through a Model Context Protocol-style tool interface. It provides a critical review of agentic evaluation along six orthogonal dimensions and identifies the industrial blind spot of current benchmarks. Finally, it proposes a multi-dimensional benchmarking framework for industrial agentic AI comprising scenario library, harness, metrics and humancalibration protocol. The paper states explicitly which components are implemented in the current prototype, which belong to the proposed reference design and which remain future work, and reports preliminary cost and latency observations from an operating site. Together, EI2ROC and the benchmarking framework constitute a methodological blueprint transferable across CAPEX intensive industries.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất kiến trúc multi-agent EI2ROC cho Trung tâm Điều hành Từ xa tích hợp trong ngành khai thác mỏ, dùng LLM orchestrator kết hợp các agent chuyên biệt qua giao diện tool kiểu MCP.
papers.llm_reason: Kiến trúc agentic với LLM orchestrator có giá trị nội dung, nhưng thiếu experiment riêng và bối cảnh mining quá hẹp để áp dụng cho solopreneur content AI.

papers.title: ECGQuest: Benchmarking and Fine-Tuning Language Models for Electrocardiography
papers.abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation requires knowledge of cardiology, electrophysiology, clinical diagnosis, ECG waveforms, signal acquisition, and instrumentation. Existing language-model benchmarks, however, primarily assess broad medical knowledge or interpretation of individual ECG signals and images rather than the broader contextual knowledge required for ECG interpretation. We developed ECGQuest, a literature-grounded resource for evaluating and fine-tuning ECG-specific language models. A GPT-4o-based pipeline generated questions from 23 ECG references and Computing in Cardiology proceedings from 2003-2025. The final dataset contains 10,904 unique True/False questions paired with their negated forms (21,808 Q&A pairs). We evaluated three commercial and 20 open-source language models on a held-out test set in a zero-shot setting. Five open-source models with 7-14B parameters were fine-tuned using Low-Rank Adaptation, with BERT and BiomedBERT included as supervised encoder baselines. Generalization was assessed on ECG-related subsets of MedMCQA and MedQA converted to binary True/False questions using official answer keys. Zero-shot accuracy on ECGQuest ranged from 49.5% to 74.4%, with GPT-5 performing best. General-purpose models outperformed medically specialized models, several models showed strong True/False bias, and encoder baselines performed near chance. Fine-tuning improved all open-source models by 6.5-14.1%. Fine-tuned DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B reached 76.3% accuracy, while a five-model voting ensemble reached 78.5%. On MedMCQA and MedQA, fine-tuning mainly benefited weaker or class-biased models and did not consistently improve strong base models. ECGQuest provides a reproducible benchmark for contextual ECG knowledge and shows that parameter-efficient fine-tuning can make smaller language models competitive with substantially larger commercial models.
papers.llm_summary: ECGQuest: benchmark 21.808 Q&A từ 23 tài liệu để đánh giá/fine-tune LM về điện tâm đồ, test 23 model.
papers.llm_reason: Benchmark QM/phương pháp luận đánh giá model có giá trị học hỏi, nhưng content ECG tim mạch gần như không liên quan đến AI content/business của bạn.

papers.title: Conflict-Aware Autonomous Resource Orchestration for 5G Edge Slicing Using Multi-Agent Systems and LLMs
papers.abstract: 5G edge network slicing must reconcile two coupled requirements: understanding high-level operator intent and reallocating scarce computing and bandwidth resources under dynamic contention. Centralized optimization can face computational and responsiveness challenges under rapidly changing edge contention, and Multi-Agent System (MAS)-based auctions can support resource arbitration but still depend on operator-defined economic parameters and priorities. Embedding a Large Language Model (LLM) directly in a recurring control loop, by contrast, may introduce non-negligible inference latency and non-deterministic behavior. This paper proposes a two-timescale architecture that addresses this gap: an LLM-based Strategist translates natural-language network intents into economic policy parameters (budget, income, and bidding-aggressiveness) at the macro scale, while a deterministic, Vickrey-inspired second-price mechanism run by SPADE-based slice agents resolves recurring resource contention at the operational scale, with the resulting allocations enforced by patching Kubernetes CPU limits and Calico CNI bandwidth annotations directly on User Plane Function pods. We evaluate the architecture end-to-end on a real Kubernetes/Open5GS edge cluster across two complementary scenarios, each repeated 30 times: a Smart-City scenario, in which natural-language public-safety intents propagate into measurable changes in slice bids and bandwidth allocations within a few auction rounds, and a Hierarchical-slicing scenario, in which the mechanism provides priority-dependent resource and QoE differentiation, adapts to abrupt demand changes, and preserves configured minimum guarantees while maintaining near-complete allocation of the shared bandwidth pool.
papers.llm_summary: Kiến trúc hai timescale: LLM Strategist chuyển intent thành tham số kinh tế, agent SPADE chạy cơ chế auction xác định trên cluster Kubernetes/Open5GS thật.
papers.llm_reason: Thực nghiệm end-to-end thật 30 lần nhưng niche 5G telecom; insight 'LLM đặt policy + code xác định thi hành' transferable được nhưng xa business/content của solopreneur.

papers.title: DPE-Rec: Diversity-Preserving and Efficient Diffusion Language Model Recommendation for Bundle Construction
papers.abstract: Generative bundle construction completes a partially observed bundle by generating its missing items from a large product catalog. Compared to autoregressive LLMs, diffusion LLM emerges as a natural fit for this unordered generation task. Their bidirectional attention provides an inductive bias better aligned with unordered bundle construction. Iterative denoising can reveal multiple tokens per step, potentially reducing inference latency. However, directly applying DLMs to this task presents two key challenges: 1 Despite its flexible reveal order, confidence-guided decoding tends to postpone semantic-fork decisions until refinement tokens constrain their choices, reducing bundle diversity. 2 Revealing more tokens per step can compromise recommendation quality, stifling the potential for faster inference. We introduce DPE-Rec, a diffusion framework for diversity preservation and efficient recommendation. DPE-Rec preserves diversity by introducing semantic-fork-aware GRPO, which prioritizes semantic-fork decisions via autoregressive rollouts. It improves efficiency through pseudo-trajectory distillation, which concentrates learning from the vast random corruption space onto the compact trajectory-induced subspace visited by high-quality decoding, unlocking reliable multi-token decoding. Together, these components enable diverse and accurate bundle construction with substantially fewer denoise steps. Experiments on multiple bundle construction benchmarks show that DPE-Rec improves recommendation performance by 63% on average, and its fast variant achieves 25.6$times$ faster inference on average than existing generative recommendation arts, with minimal loss in recommendation quality.
papers.llm_summary: DPE-Rec là framework diffusion LLM cho bundle recommendation, dùng semantic-fork-aware GRPO để giữ diversity và pseudo-trajectory distillation để tăng hiệu quả inference khi xây dựng gợi ý combo sản phẩm.
papers.llm_reason: Recommendation/bundling có liên quan business nhưng phương pháp diffusion LLM cho bundle construction quá chuyên sâu, ít actionable trực tiếp cho solopreneur làm content.

papers.title: FairTest: Search-Based Fairness Testing for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) trains a team of agents that share one environment and learn their policies together. Training maximizes the team return, and a high return does not imply that the rewards are shared fairly among the agents in every episode. Testing is an established way to discover the failures of deep reinforcement learning, yet few methods address the fairness of MARL. In this work, we propose FairTest, a search-based testing approach that seeks the unfair executions of a MARL policy. The design combines search guidance with test prioritization. The guidance scores each candidate with three fitness functions. One measures the fairness of the runs already performed, another predicts the fairness from abstract states and fairness features, and the third reads the decision uncertainty from the policy. Crossover and mutation derive further candidates from the observed executions. The prioritization ranks the candidates by the predicted fairness and the decision uncertainty, so that the runs reach the candidates where failures are expected. FairTest is evaluated on three environments and two MARL algorithms, and four baselines are given the same budget. It detects the most fairness failures compared to three baselines with statistical significance and large effect sizes. The failure count exceeds that of the strongest baseline by 221% on average and coverage improves by an average of 23%.
papers.llm_summary: FairTest dùng search-based testing với 3 fitness function để phát hiện unfair executions trong hệ thống Multi-Agent RL.
papers.llm_reason: MARL core nhưng quá学术/testing, experiment có ý nghĩa thống kê nhưng ít actionable cho content/business.

papers.title: ULME: Predictive Coupling for Mutually Reinforcing Embedding and Language Modeling
papers.abstract: Text embedding and text generation are two of the most useful capabilities of modern large language models, yet they are typically provided by separate specialized models (an embedder and a generator) trained with incompatible objectives and deployed side by side in retrieval-augmented generation and agent systems. Recent unified embedding-generation models such as GritLM share parameters between the two capabilities, but they either switch attention regimes between modes or optimize embedding and language modeling as parallel objectives that never supervise each other. We argue that these designs are only partially unified: the two capabilities coexist on the same weights, but do not shape each other. We propose ULME, a post-training framework that unifies embedding and language modeling on a causal decoder-only LLM through predictive coupling. ULME inserts a chain of learnable slots between the query and the answer, reads a semantic embedding and a reasoning embedding from two designated slots, and trains three objectives on a shared causal backbone: a contrastive loss anchoring the semantic slot to document representations, a language-modeling loss supervising answer generation, and a stop-gradient predictive loss that aligns the reasoning slot with a pooled summary of the answer, so that generation actively shapes what the embedding encodes. Across two model families (Qwen2.5, Qwen3) and eight scales spanning 0.5B-8B parameters, a single ULME checkpoint improves MTEB by 3.3-4.1 points over the strongest open-source baseline, tightens BRIGHT and AdvBench-IR simultaneously, and remains on par with a generation-only fine-tune on standard accuracy benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, MMLU-Pro, HumanEval), demonstrating that genuine unification yields mutually reinforcing rather than merely coexisting capabilities.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất ULME, framework post-training thống nhất embedding và language modeling trên cùng một decoder-only LLM thông qua predictive coupling, giúp generation chủ động định hình embedding.
papers.llm_reason: Liên quan cốt lõi AI/LLM nhưng rất thiên về kiến trúc mô hình, ít ứng dụng trực tiếp cho content/business; insight hành động thấp cho solopreneur.

papers.title: Learning Robust Personalized Prompts for LLM-Driven Sequential Recommendation
papers.abstract: LLM-driven sequential recommendation formulates next-item prediction as autoregressive generation conditioned on natural-language prompts. However, minor wording changes in semantically equivalent prompts can cause substantial performance fluctuations, undermining robustness and requiring costly manual prompt engineering. Continuous prompt learning reduces template dependence but faces two interacting challenges: shared task-level instructions lack user-specific reasoning guidance, while gradient updates can push continuous prompts outside the LLM's effective semantic space. Injecting personalized signals can further amplify this semantic drift. To address these challenges, we propose LRPRec, a learnable prompting framework that initializes continuous instruction prompts from discrete templates and introduces two complementary mechanisms. Personalized prompt injection encodes user behavior into a preference embedding and additively injects it into shared prompts, enabling parameter-efficient user-level adaptation. A semantic drift constraint regularizes the shared prompts within a trust region around their initialization anchors to preserve semantic validity during optimization. By constraining the shared component while allowing additive personalization, LRPRec decouples stability from expressiveness. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over strong baselines while eliminating the need for manual tuning of background and task inference templates.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất LRPRec, framework học personalized continuous prompts cho recommendation dựa trên LLM, giải quyết vấn đề robustness khi wording thay đổi và semantic drift.
papers.llm_reason: Liên quan LLM prompting và personalization, có experiment trên 3 benchmark, nhưng recommendation system không phải trọng tâm content/business của solopreneur; insight hạn chế.

papers.title: CovNav: Conformal Prediction-Guided Adaptive Inference for Object Goal Navigation
papers.abstract: In object goal navigation (ObjectNav), an embodied agent must find a target object (e.g., "find a bed") in a previously unseen environment, relying on spatial commonsense such as object co-occurrence. Large Language Models (LLMs) encode this commonsense, but deploying them on robots exposes a trade-off between reasoning quality and efficiency: cloud-based models incur latency and privacy risks, whereas small on-device LLMs are fast but prone to hallucinated spatial judgments. Hybrid reasoning LLMs offer both a fast non-thinking mode and a slow thinking mode, which raises a key question for embodied agents: when is slow thinking worth its cost? We propose CovNav, a training-free framework that answers this question with Conformal Prediction (CP), turning dual-process (System 1 / System 2) inference into an uncertainty-aware decision. Much like recent decision models such as Jev, CovNav casts each spatial query as a structured binary decision rather than free-form generation: a local LLM in fast mode judges whether the target is likely near an observed object, CP converts its token probabilities into a prediction set, and only ambiguous queries are escalated to slow chain-of-thought reasoning. The object-pair formulation keeps calibration tractable and supports open-set objects through off-the-shelf detectors. Experiments on Gibson and HM3D show that CovNav surpasses the strongest zero-shot baseline by 0.8 and 1.7 percentage points in success rate on HM3D v1 and v2, while invoking slow reasoning for only 12.4% of queries and retaining most of the gain of always-on thinking at a fraction of its latency. Real-robot experiments on a TurtleBot 4 further validate the approach. CovNav shows how calibrated uncertainty can decide when an embodied agent should think slowly, offering a principled form of adaptive test-time reasoning for LLM-based robots.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất CovNav, dùng Conformal Prediction để quyết định khi nào nên chuyển từ suy nghĩ nhanh (fast mode) sang suy nghĩ chậm (slow CoT) trong tác tử điều hướng vật thể trên robot.
papers.llm_reason: Ý tưởng fast/slow thinking với uncertainty-aware escalation rất hay để làm content về agent, nhưng bối cảnh robotics hẹp và ít liên quan trực tiếp đến business/content, điểm thực tiễn bị giới hạn.

papers.title: VACS: Value-Aligned Compositional Shielding for Multi-Agent Reasoning
papers.abstract: Multi-agent reasoning systems in high-stakes domains must be both accurate and safe, yet agents often follow heterogeneous value priorities (e.g., rigor, conciseness, safety), causing conflicting recommendations. Existing methods do not jointly provide: (i) principled inference of each agent's implicit values from behavior, (ii) compositional formal safety guarantees without full online communication, and (iii) value-aware conflict resolution with faithful explanations. We present VACS (Value-Aligned Compositional Shielding), a four-layer framework addressing all three. Layer 1 learns value-dimension rewards from pairwise preferences using Bradley-Terry modeling and infers per-agent value weights via deep MaxEnt IRL. Layer 2 encodes value constraints in a Lean-inspired DSL and synthesizes compositional assume-guarantee shields for runtime safety. Layer 3 resolves disagreement through nucleolus-based credit allocation and Hamiltonian consensus optimization under long-term value constraints. Layer 4 extracts a critical reasoning path from co-state sensitivities and generates formally grounded natural-language explanations. Our contribution is primarily a unified systems design with formalized interfaces and operational guarantees at the verifier-constrained decision level, rather than a complete end-to-end formal proof of all language-model internals. In controlled proof-of-concept evaluations with role-conditioned agent panels on NEJM-AI QA, MathInstruct-Subset, and a cybersecurity incident-response benchmark (CyberSec-Eval), VACS outperforms strong baselines in accuracy (85.4%, 95.0%, and 90.0%) while reducing logical inconsistency rates to near zero.
papers.llm_summary: VACS khung 4 lớp căn chỉnh giá trị, đảm bảo an toàn hình thức và giải thích xung đột trong multi-agent reasoning.
papers.llm_reason: Chỉ proof-of-concept kiểm soát, thiết kế hệ thống hình thức nặng lý thuyết, khó chuyển thành hành động cho người làm content AI.

papers.title: A Survey on LLM-Integrated Hardware Design Verification
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being integrated into hardware verification to automate specification interpretation, verification-artifact generation, debugging, formal reasoning, and tool orchestration. This survey provides a systematic review of LLM-assisted hardware functional verification across SystemVerilog assertion generation, stimulus and testbench generation, bug localization and design repair, model checking and equivalence checking, SAT/SMT optimization, and emerging agentic verification workflows. We organize the literature by methodology, verification objective, tool interaction, benchmark, and evaluation criterion, and examine both inference-time techniques--including prompting, retrieval, structured reasoning, and agentic workflows--and training-time adaptation. Across these areas, a common pattern emerges: LLMs are most effective as semantic reasoning, search, and orchestration components embedded within verification-aware workflows, while simulators, formal engines, coverage tools, and solvers provide executable feedback and correctness evidence. However, tool acceptance alone does not establish verification correctness, since assertions, tests, repairs, or proofs may satisfy available checks without faithfully capturing the complete design intent. We therefore identify semantic alignment between specifications and verification evidence, scalable integration with deterministic tools, generalization to unseen designs, and rigorous evaluation of correctness, cost, robustness, and human effort as key challenges. Finally, we discuss emerging directions toward specification-centered, neuro-symbolic, and persistent agentic verification systems that combine LLM flexibility with independently checkable verification evidence.
papers.llm_summary: Survey tổng quan LLM tích hợp vào hardware verification: sinh assertion, testbench, debug, agentic workflow.
papers.llm_reason: Là survey không experiment mới, domain EDA hẹp, chỉ có ích như bản đồ xu hướng agentic workflow cho nhà nghiên cứu.

papers.title: Transformers as Generic Deep Neural Networks: Exact Compilation, the Cost of Removing Activation-Activation Products, and Multi-Agent Attention Clustering
papers.abstract: Transformers are deployed as a special model class. Neural processing units (NPU) add dedicated operators for attention and normalization, and quantization relies on Transformer-specific algorithms. We show the computation does not force this. Every Transformer block, with attention, LayerNorm and a GELU MLP, compiles exactly into a generic deep neural network built from fixed affine maps, routing and the square, sigmoid and inverse square root, plus GELU or its sigmoid approximation. Without activation-activation products, every transform-wise compilation adds at least $N^2$ scalar nonlinear evaluations per head for dense scores. Keeping that one operation type removes this cost; its elementwise form, present on every surveyed NPU, suffices with the sigmoid and inverse square root. For top-$k$ attention with exchangeable tail scores, we prove that exact or conditional-mean tail mass gives an unbiased, minimum-mean-square-error estimate of the attention distribution, while tail drop is conditionally biased. When queries or agents cluster, centroids choose the keys first, reducing the number of computed scores from $N^2$ to $Nk$ per head. On DeiT-Tiny, MambaIRv2-Light and Pythia-70M the compiled models match their references with all keys, standard post-training quantization applies, and the exact tail-mass estimate beats tail dropping with half as many keys on DeiT-Tiny and, for $k\le8$, on Pythia-70M.
papers.llm_summary: Chứng minh Transformer biên dịch chính xác thành DNN generic, tối ưu cost nonlinearity và attention clustering cho NPU.
papers.llm_reason: Lý thuyết biên dịch/quantization có experiment nhỏ DeiT-Tiny/Pythia, gần như không actionable cho làm content hay business AI.

papers.title: Embedding Subspace Partitioning for Dynamic Multi-Objective Retrieval
papers.abstract: Modern industrial recommender systems must optimize across competing objectives, balancing semantic relevance with business metrics such as engagement and revenue. While bi-encoders dominate large-scale retrieval due to their efficiency, they collapse these heterogeneous signals into a single static embedding space. This design creates a fundamental limitation: once trained, the retriever cannot adapt to shifting objective priorities at serving time without retraining. Moreover, joint optimization with multi-objective losses often induces interference between objectives, leading to suboptimal trade-offs. We propose Embedding Subspace Partitioning (ESP), a retrieval framework that decomposes the embedding into task-aware subspaces and replaces the single dot product with a weighted sum of per-subspace similarities, whose weights are tunable at serving time. For Transformer bi-encoders, ESP uses the model's native end-of-sequence token as a segment delimiter, with segment-aware attention masking and position encoding resets to guarantee subspace isolation in a single forward pass. Serving is performed via GPU-accelerated exhaustive kNN over one concatenated index, eliminating the need for per-objective Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) infrastructure required by multi-head approaches. We evaluate ESP on an open-source benchmark built from MS MARCO. A single ESP model traces a broad Pareto frontier, consistently outperforming strong multi-task baselines across diverse operating points. In LinkedIn's job matching platform (70M+ weekly users), ESP enabled dynamic retrieval reconfiguration and delivered significant key business metric lifts.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất ESP phân hoạch embedding thành các subspace theo mục tiêu, cho phép điều chỉnh trọng số đa mục tiêu lúc phục vụ mà không cần retrain, đánh giá trên benchmark MS MARCO.
papers.llm_reason: Có liên quan business metrics (engagement, revenue) và benchmark thực, nhưng là kỹ thuật embedding/retrieval truyền thống không phải LLM/agent, insight quá kỹ thuật cho content creator.

papers.title: Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment for LLM Reasoning over Temporal Knowledge Graphs
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) often struggle with temporally grounded reasoning because their static parametric memory is misaligned with the dynamic evolution of real-world knowledge. Although RAG and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) provide practical ways to enhance LLMs, they remain insufficient for temporal reasoning. Existing retrieval methods typically prioritize semantic relevance while overlooking temporal validity, event order, and evolutionary dependencies, resulting in evidence that is relevant in isolation but temporally fragmented. Meanwhile, conventional PEFT methods usually employ fixed and input-agnostic low-rank updates, making it difficult to capture time-dependent entity semantics and relation drift. To address these limitations, we propose Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment (TEPCA), a framework for LLM reasoning over TKGs. TEPCA aligns LLM reasoning with temporal knowledge at both the evidence and parameter levels. At the evidence level, it introduces time-constrained Dynamic Relevance-Guided Path (DRGP) pruning to preserve globally coherent temporal paths, together with Mutual-Information (MI)-based pruning to retain query-informative local facts under temporal constraints. At the parameter level, it integrates Dynamic-Gated LoRA (DG-LoRA), a timestamp-conditioned low-rank adaptation mechanism that dynamically modulates the effective adaptation subspace according to temporal context. This design enables LLMs to better capture fine-grained entity evolution and time-dependent relation semantics while preserving parameter efficiency. Experimental results on two TKG benchmarks demonstrate that TEPCA achieves state-of-the-art performance. Additional evaluations of DG-LoRA on eight commonsense QA datasets further verify its general input-adaptive capacity, scalability across LLM backbones, and interpretability.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất TEPCA căn chỉnh bằng chứng và tham số theo thời gian (RAG pruning temporal + DG-LoRA điều kiện timestamp) để LLM reasoning trên temporal knowledge graph.
papers.llm_reason: Core LLM/RAG nhưng quá chuyên sâu temporal KG, thực nghiệm ít được mô tả rõ và gần như không liên quan business/content hay actionable với solopreneur.

papers.title: IMPACT: Intent-driven Multi-agent Policy with Attention for SLO-guaranteed Microservice Migration in Cloud-edge Systems
papers.abstract: Ensuring strict tail-latency service-level objectives (SLOs) in dynamic mobile edge computing (MEC) systems remains challenging because user mobility, wireless fading, bursty workloads, and partial observability jointly undermine reliable cloud-edge orchestration. Existing microservice migration methods predominantly optimize average delay and often decouple migration from bandwidth control, leading to uncoordinated decisions, queue oscillation, and frequent high-percentile latency violations. To address this issue, we propose IMPACT, an intent-driven Agentic AI framework for cooperative microservice migration and bandwidth control in cloud-edge systems. Under centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE), each edge cloud is modeled as an autonomous agent that encodes local SLO risk, migration urgency, and computational pressure into compact, semantic intent representations. IMPACT further introduces a double-attention mechanism that first selectively aggregates relevant peer intents for efficient inter-agent communication and then filters local observations to emphasize goal-relevant state information. This design enables robust coordination under partial observability and jointly optimizes service migration and discrete uplink bandwidth allocation. Extensive experiments in 5-edge and 20-edge scenarios show that IMPACT reduces mean latency by 30-50% and tail-latency deviation by 40-70% compared with state-of-the-art factorized multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) and heuristic baselines, while achieving near-zero SLO violation rates under tight thresholds and energy consumption close to the best heuristic baseline. These results demonstrate that intent-driven agentic coordination provides an effective and scalable solution for SLO-aware orchestration in complex cloud-edge intelligent systems.
papers.llm_summary: IMPACT dùng agentic AI multi-agent CTDE với double-attention và intent representation để migration microservice + điều phối bandwidth cloud-edge đảm bảo SLO tail-latency.
papers.llm_reason: Có agentic multi-agent nhưng thiên infra cloud-edge (20), experiment 5/20-edge giảm latency 30-50% thật (18), xa business/marketing/content (6) và insight dành engineer infra, ít dùng cho creator (6).

papers.title: MAS-Gate: Unlocking Multi-Agent System Lifecycle via Node-Centric Quantification
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) can solve complex problems beyond the reach of a single agent by decomposing tasks and coordinating complementary capabilities. Despite extensive research on MAS, existing work largely focuses on specific aspects or individual phases of their development and operation, resulting in fragmented perspectives with objectives and signals that are difficult to reconcile across these different settings. To bridge these disconnected perspectives, we conceptualize MAS development and operation as a three-phase lifecycle spanning design-time orchestration before execution, runtime intervention during execution, and post-hoc attribution after execution, and introduce MAS-Gate, a unified node-centric quantification applicable across these phases. Modeling each execution as a directed acyclic graph, MAS-Gate combines within-node utility, which estimates a node's contribution through changes in reference-answer likelihood, with inter-node strength, which approximates semantic uptake and potential downstream reach. We adapt this shared quantification to three objectives: providing a structure-aware dense reward for Orchestrator training, training an Editor to act on execution prefixes using paired rewards from completed edited and unedited trajectories, and supplying risk-ranked nodes as auxiliary evidence for LLM-based post-hoc attribution. Experiments spanning interaction environments, knowledge-intensive multi-hop question answering, general reasoning, and post-hoc attribution demonstrate that MAS-Gate improves workflow construction, targeted runtime editing, and LLM-assisted error localization over corresponding phase-specific baselines. Together, these results establish MAS-Gate as a unified structural interface for improving MAS generation, dynamic editing, and error attribution throughout the lifecycle.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất MAS-Gate, framework quantification node-centric thống nhất toàn bộ lifecycle của multi-agent system (design-time, runtime, post-hoc) để đánh giá contribution và tối ưu hóa.
papers.llm_reason: Liên quan MAS nhưng mang tính phương pháp luận học thuật cao, ít experiment cụ thể trong abstract, gần như không có insight hành động trực tiếp cho content creator.

papers.title: QuantumMind: Constraint-Grounded Agentic Reasoning for Speedup Analysis in Quantum Computing
papers.abstract: Identifying a meaningful quantum speedup requires more than matching a classical problem to a familiar quantum primitive: the claim must preserve the task, respect access and output models, expose required promises, and remain within a defensible complexity scope. We present QuantumMind, an auditable agentic workflow for generating and conservatively screening quantum-acceleration hypotheses. A fixed sequence of typed, role-specialized actions formalizes the public task, analyzes structure and classical bottlenecks, matches a source-linked registry of quantum primitives and barriers, and constructs a scoped candidate scheme. A deterministic ten-check validator assigns the authoritative verdict; completed states are compiled into a Quantum Acceleration Evidence Graph and passed through a downward-only research screen that cannot strengthen the decision. We evaluate QuantumMind against seven task-adapted prompting and agentic controls on 582 identical open-discovery tasks. Under the frozen Open-Discovery Score (ODS), QuantumMind obtains 53.1 mean ODS, exceeding the strongest baseline by 17.3 points (48.2% relative), and wins 355 of 582 paired tasks against that baseline. It passes the graph audit on 99.8% of tasks, compared with 43.6% for the strongest baseline, and ranks first in all seven task families. The results indicate that typed state transitions and deterministic evidence control contribute beyond fluent generation alone.
papers.llm_summary: Xây dựng QuantumMind, một workflow agentic có validator xác định (deterministic) để sàng lọc giả thuyết tăng tốc lượng tử, đạt ODS 53.1 vượt baseline 17.3 điểm trên 582 tác vụ.
papers.llm_reason: Thiết kế agentic workflow với typed actions và deterministic validator đáng chú ý, experiment tốt, nhưng chủ đề quantum computing quá xa rời nội dung content/business AI phổ thông.

papers.title: SpecRead: A Benchmark for Measuring Whether Language Models Understand Hardware Specifications
papers.abstract: Existing benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) in hardware design evaluate downstream artifacts such as generated RTL, assertions, or testbenches. When a model fails such a benchmark, the failure is ambiguous: it may have misread the specification, or it may have understood the specification and failed to write the code. We present SpecRead, a benchmark that isolates specification comprehension from generation ability. SpecRead v2.1 contains 385 questions over 10 open-source OpenTitan IP blocks: exact retrieval, cross-section reasoning, contradiction detection in mutated specifications, and spec-RTL consistency checking, plus 82 controls (41 distractor, 41 consistent-RTL). Type-4 items are built from real RTL mutations; we retain only mutations that Icarus Verilog simulation shows to change observable behavior. A with-spec vs. without-spec ablation suggests the questions require the excerpt, not training recall alone (without-spec accuracy 3/20 on the t1/t2 subset), though memorization of the source text may still help spot mutations. As an initial characterization with a small model, Ministral-3B scores 33.2% overall (128/385; macro average 39.0%): 55.2% on retrieval, 51.7% on cross-section reasoning. On the two contradiction-focused types, the verdict-plus-location measure gives 48.0% (t3) and 63.3% (t4), with a 51.2% false-positive rate on distractors and 100% on consistent-RTL controls. Layered scoring shows the model locates contradictions well (78.9-81.6% location accuracy) but scores lower on their category (43.9-49.7%). A structured "rule-table" prompting intervention lowers accuracy on every question type except t2 (tied). SpecRead is automatically scorable by deterministic checks, with gray-zone cases counted wrong under the conservative main scoring. The benchmark is regenerable for type-3 items via mutation injection, and built exclusively from public sources.
papers.llm_summary: SpecRead là benchmark 385 câu hỏi tách 'hiểu spec' khỏi 'viết code' để đo comprehension hardware spec của LLM trên OpenTitan.
papers.llm_reason: Benchmark LLM chất lượng với ablation có thật và ý tưởng đánh giá hữu ích, nhưng domain hardware design xa rời nội dung marketing/chess/30+.

papers.title: A Channel-Boosted Multi-Agent System with Iterative Consultation for Document Sensitivity Classification
papers.abstract: Organizations in critical national infrastructure sectors must assess heterogeneous documents for sensitivity before routing or storage. Manual assessment is slow, inconsistent, and unscalable. Extending our prior leakage-controlled benchmark, BERT established the top single-encoder baseline (89.14% accuracy, 89.33% F1-score under 5-fold cross-validation on the Strategic 16K corpus). However, transformer baselines suffer from a structural limitation: fixed input length truncation discards evidence beyond the retained window-precisely where sensitive cables tend to be longest. We present Channel-Boosted MAS (CB-MAS) and instantiate it as IC-MAS (Iterative Consultation Multi-Agent System) to solve this without long-context computational costs. A Channel Critic Agent learns document-adaptive trust weights governing Gated Channel Boosting between two first-window encoders, while paired Consultation Agents iteratively exchange belief states to reconcile evidence from the beginning and end of long documents. IC-MAS holds computation constant regardless of document length by reconciling fixed windows in a compact representation space. Ablation studies show critic-controlled Channel Boosting provides the bulk of accuracy gains, while consultation recovers recall without precision collapse. Critic-Controlled Gated Channel Boosting with Max-Pool fusion and Blackboard Adaptive Consultation achieves 90.72% accuracy, 91.23% F1-score, 92.01% sensitive recall, and 90.46% sensitive precision, using about 54% less average computation than a fixed-round baseline. Gains over the single-encoder baseline are statistically significant (McNemar's test, p less than 0.000001; paired t-test). We include LIME/SHAP explainability, multi-agent evaluation, and an honest accounting of limitations.
papers.llm_summary: Channel-Boosted Multi-Agent System (IC-MAS) phân loại độ nhạy cảm tài liệu dài bằng cách kết hợp gated channel boosting giữa hai encoder và iterative consultation giữa các agent, giữ computation cố định bất kể độ dài văn bản.
papers.llm_reason: Multi-agent có experiment thật trên corpus 16K nhưng bài toán phân loại tài liệu nhạy cảm trong hạ tầng quốc gia quá niche, gần như không liên quan đến solopreneur content AI.

papers.title: DreamTest: World-Model Surrogates for Search-Based Testing of Deep Reinforcement Learning Agents
papers.abstract: Testing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agents in cyber-physical systems aims to uncover diverse failures before deployment, but each execution can be expensive. Surrogate-assisted testing reduces this cost by learning to predict which test configurations are likely to fail. Prior surrogates treat the system as a black box and predict pass or fail outcomes directly; we instead model how a test unfolds and estimate failure from an imagined episode. We introduce DreamTest, a world-model surrogate for testing DRL agents. DreamTest adapts a recurrent state-space model to learn agent behaviour and environment dynamics from the agent's training log. Given a candidate configuration, imagined rollouts produce a failure score that guides search without executing every candidate in a simulator or real system. We evaluate DreamTest for failure prediction, test generation, and failure diversity on Parking, Humanoid, and DonkeyCar. Mean area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) exceeds the strongest baseline by 97%, 12%, and 39%, respectively, and gains on five out-of-distribution test sets reach 145%, 29%, and 44%. Under the same simulator-validation budget, the best "DreamTest + search" combinations find 29%, 22%, and 79% more novel failures on average. Across clusterings with k = 2-40, failures generated with DreamTest cover the most behavioural clusters for almost all k, indicating that DreamTest consistently discovers behaviourally diverse failures.
papers.llm_summary: Dùng world-model (recurrent state-space model) học từ log huấn luyện để 'tưởng tượng' episode và dự đoán thất bại của DRL agent, giảm chi phí kiểm thử trong hệ thống cyber-physical.
papers.llm_reason: Thí nghiệm mạnh trên 3 domain với AUPRC/chết-dị thường vượt baseline tới 145%, nhưng là testing DRL chuyên sâu, ít nối với content/business AI của solopreneur.

papers.title: UniCon: A Unified Context-Centric Modeling Paradigm for CTR Prediction
papers.abstract: Unified modeling has become a major direction for industrial click-through rate (CTR) prediction. Existing approaches typically unify sequential and non-sequential signals at the token level, model their interactions in a shared backbone, and increase model capacity to improve scaling behavior. However, this division originates from legacy feature-engineering practice and is misaligned with the underlying decision process. User behavior is inherently a sequence of homogeneous context units; at the level of input organization, historical behavior and the current request differ only in whether their outcomes are observed or remain to be predicted. Treating them as heterogeneous signals obscures structural dependencies within the user's decision context, limiting both scaling efficiency and prediction quality. This limitation is particularly pronounced in context-rich scenarios such as e-commerce shelves and waterfall feeds. To address this, we propose UniCon, a unified context-centric modeling architecture that treats the request context as the basic modeling unit and organizes history and prediction targets as homogeneous context units. Intra-context attention captures local coupling among items within a context (Locality), while inter-context attention models the dynamic evolution of decision states across contexts (Dynamics). This organization bridges the structural gap between history and target and supports more effective scaling of unified CTR models. Context-unit-level sequence compression further reduces deployment overhead. On Meituan search advertising, UniCon improves offline AUC by 0.0139 over a strong production baseline and achieves statistically significant online lifts of 3.09% in RPM, 2.07% in CTR, and 2.95% in revenue.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất UniCon, kiến trúc mô hình hóa thống nhất theo context cho dự đoán CTR, tổ chức history và prediction target thành các context unit đồng nhất với attention nội và liên context.
papers.llm_reason: Liên quan business (CTR, e-commerce) nhưng là mô hình ML truyền thống không phải LLM/agent, kỹ thuật sâu và ít insight hành động trực tiếp cho solopreneur làm content.

papers.title: IFC-MCQ: Automatically Generating Multiple-Choice Benchmarks for Evaluating LLM Agents on IFC Data Retrieval
papers.abstract: Industry Foundation Classes (IFC), the standard for building information exchange in architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC), is increasingly queried through large language models (LLMs) using natural language. Evaluating these systems at scale is difficult because free-text answers require costly human or LLM-based review. We propose IFC-MCQ, a method that automatically generates multiple-choice benchmarks from IFC files for exact option-set grading. The taxonomy covers 15 categories and 36 subtypes across four groups, with answer keys derived from the file and distractors constructed from file-derived values or predefined rules. We applied IFC-MCQ to IFC models of varying sizes and modelling characteristics to assess generation coverage and evaluated two agentic configurations on selected models using tool- and code-based retrieval. The evaluation exposed category-specific failure modes and showed that performance can vary with the source IFC model and retrieval interface. IFC-MCQ enables scalable benchmarking of LLM-based IFC retrieval in AEC workflows.
papers.llm_summary: IFC-MCQ tự động tạo benchmark trắc nghiệm từ file IFC để đánh giá LLM agent truy xuất dữ liệu trong ngành xây dựng (AEC) với grading chính xác.
papers.llm_reason: Phương pháp benchmark hóa agent có experiment thật, nhưng domain AEC quá hẹp và gần như không liên quan content cờ tướng/30+ hay business cá nhân.

papers.title: From Codebase to Culprit (C2C): Reducing the Search Space for Bugs with Semantic Retrieval and Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce C2C (From Codebase to Culprit), a framework for precise bug localization that progressively reduces the debugging search space across multiple levels of granularity: files, functions, and lines of code. To mirror developer's natural top-down debugging workflows, C2C integrates semantic retrieval and Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) in a two-stage process. First, it performs recall-oriented retrieval of buggy candidates via semantic vector similarity search using bug-report text, including available stack-trace information, against a database of embeddings, where the embeddings are fine-tuned via contrastive learning with CodeBERT. Building on this reduced search space, the HRL framework incrementally localizes bugs, reasoning from files to functions and ultimately to individual lines of code. Unlike prior approaches which operate at a single granularity, C2C enables multi-resolution localization while maintaining contextual consistency across decisions. Experiments on real-world Java and Python datasets demonstrate that C2C improves retrieval precision and localization accuracy. Ablation studies further highlight the contributions of hierarchical decomposition, structured learning signals, and reward shaping in advancing multi-level bug localization.
papers.llm_summary: C2C là framework định vị bug theo phân cấp file→function→line bằng semantic retrieval với CodeBERT embeddings và hierarchical reinforcement learning, mô phỏng quy trình debugging tự nhiên của developer.
papers.llm_reason: Có experiment thật trên Java/Python datasets nhưng bug localization quá niche, ít liên quan đến business/content AI và không tạo insight hành động rõ ràng cho solopreneur.

papers.title: WaitLens: Temporal VLM-Based Adaptive Waiting for Industrial GUI Testing Agents
papers.abstract: Improving the efficiency of GUI testing agents is important for industrial deployment. Beyond LLM inference, fixed waiting between consecutive interactions introduces substantial overhead. Our industrial study reveals that fixed waiting accounts for 42.3% of the time within the sampled interaction intervals, comparable to the 54.8% spent on model calls. Moreover, 62.9% of the waiting time is spent after the GUI has already finished loading. Although prior studies have proposed adaptive waiting strategies, their reliance on app-specific data or platform-specific information limits their applicability across diverse industrial environments. To this end, we propose WaitLens, which fine-tunes a lightweight VLM on GUI loading trajectories annotated with waiting end times. We introduce temporal resampling to construct diverse training examples, enabling the model to learn varying GUI loading behaviors from temporal observations. Experiments show that WaitLens achieves 86.08% accuracy in deciding whether to keep waiting, compared with 54.13% for the backbone VLM. Our evaluation using recordings from Meituan's industrial testing pipeline shows that WaitLens reduces mean extra waiting after the interface is ready by 94.98% compared with a 20-second fixed wait.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất WaitLens, fine-tune VLM nhẹ để quyết định thời điểm dừng chờ trong GUI testing agent, giảm 94.98% thời gian chờ thừa so với fixed wait trên pipeline công nghiệp Meituan.
papers.llm_reason: Có experiment công nghiệp thực tế ấn tượng, liên quan GUI agent nhưng domain testing hẹp, ít liên quan content/business/marketing và insight áp dụng hạn chế cho solopreneur.

papers.title: LLMs in Cloud: A Discussion on Architecture, Orchestration, and Inference
papers.abstract: The widespread deployment of foundational Large Language Models (LLM) across cloud datacenters marks a fundamental paradigm shift from stateless deep learning toward distributed, memory-intensive generative workloads. However, serving massive foundation models under stringent Service Level Objectives (SLO) exposes critical physical and system bottlenecks. These challenges include the persistent High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) wall, operational asymmetry between compute-bound prefilling and memory-bandwidth-bound decoding, explosive Key-Value (KV) cache expansion, prohibitive serverless cold starts, and hardware reliability vulnerabilities. Existing literature reviews remain layer-siloed, decoupling low-level accelerator virtualization from cluster orchestration and runtime inference, while largely overlooking defining advancements from 2024 to 2026. To address these limitations, this study presents a comprehensive, cross-layer systematic review guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 framework. We synthesize a holistic taxonomy unifying hardware virtualization, cluster-level scheduling, and runtime inference optimizations, including iteration-level continuous batching, prefill-decoding disaggregation, and hierarchical KV cache offloading. Furthermore, we evaluate resilient cloud-native service architectures, examining scale-to-zero serverless paradigms, fault-tolerant checkpointing against silent data corruption, and hardware-enforced Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) for multi-tenant isolation. Finally, we formalize the multi-dimensional Pareto trade-offs governing throughput, latency, monetary cost, and confidentiality, outlining a forward-looking research roadmap spanning Compute Express Link (CXL) memory pooling, in-memory computing, and autonomous multi-agent control planes to guide future cloud LLM infrastructure.

papers.title: Human-Feedback-Guided Multi-Agent Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Interactive Driving Behavior Modeling
papers.abstract: Modeling human driving behavior is fundamental to understanding driver decision-making and supporting autonomous vehicles (AVs) in mixed traffic. Reward learning offers a principled way to infer the latent objectives behind driving behaviors, yet most existing methods are formulated in single-agent settings and treat surrounding vehicles as dynamic obstacles. Directly extending reward learning to multi-agent scenarios is difficult because the joint action space grows exponentially with the number of interacting vehicles. In addition, existing approaches mainly rely on physical demonstrations and rarely exploit human feedback during reward recovery. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Human-Feedback-Guided Multi-Agent Inverse Reinforcement Learning (HFG-MAIRL) framework for interactive driving behavior modeling. First, we develop a multi-agent maximum-entropy inverse reinforcement learning module that explicitly models each vehicle and its directly interacting neighbors in a localized Markov game, while using aggregated traffic states to capture the influence of the broader traffic environment. The resulting coupled multi-vehicle responses are approximated through finite marginal-response iterations over factorized vehicle-level policies, avoiding explicit enumeration of the full joint action space. Second, we incorporate human feedback as ordinal preference supervision through a Bradley-Terry likelihood. In our experiments, driver emotion labels are used as one instantiation of such feedback and converted into pairwise ordinal preference constraints. Experiments on the AIDE dataset show that HFG-MAIRL outperforms representative IRL baselines in decision modeling and produces interpretable feedback-aligned reward patterns.
papers.llm_summary: HFG-MAIRL dùng human feedback ordinal làm reward supervisor cho multi-agent inverse RL mô hình hành vi lái xe tương tác.

papers.title: Unlocking the Specialization Capability of PPG Foundation Models for Wearable Signals through Structured Pruning and Adaptive Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Photoplethysmography (PPG) plays a central role in wearable health monitoring and clinical decision support. However, existing approaches to universal PPG representation learning are predominantly trained on high-quality large-scale datasets obtained from oximeters in hospital settings and often struggle to adapt to sparse and low-quality real-world datasets, thereby limiting their generalization to clinically relevant tasks on prevalent PPG data such as collected from wearable devices. Surprisingly, even after full fine-tuning, PPG foundation models cannot consistently outperform general-purpose time-series models. Therefore, a key question is how to effectively adapt PPG foundation models to target prediction tasks. Through empirical studies on various PPG foundation models, we find that pretrained models often exhibit inherent sparsity and computational redundancy, suggesting that PPG foundation models have learned to activate task-relevant network substructures for different prediction tasks. To preserve this valuable prior knowledge, we propose a structured pruning-and-fine-tuning framework, SPAFT, which regularizes the adaptive fine-tuning process by constraining it to a more relevant and compact parameter space based on parameter importance and structural redundancy. Extensive experiments across four PPG foundation models, five benchmark datasets, and ten downstream tasks demonstrate that SPAFT achieves win rates of 82.8% and 87.5% on regression and classification tasks, respectively. This prune-then-finetune paradigm often enables PPG foundation models to achieve state-of-the-art performance, laying a promising foundation for the real-world clinical deployment of PPG foundation models and the development of personalized PPG foundation models.
papers.llm_summary: SPAFT kết hợp structured pruning + adaptive fine-tuning để chuyên biệt hóa PPG foundation models cho tín hiệu wearable, test trên 4 model 5 dataset 10 task.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration with the Common-Sense Reasoning Capabilities of LLMs for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Autonomous vehicles require robust perception and decision-making capabilities to operate in diverse and unseen scenarios. While reinforcement learning and rule-based methods can provide effective control and safety mechanisms, their performance may degrade in situations requiring contextual reasoning. Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in understanding multimodal information and generating contextual reasoning, however, their use for direct vehicle control can introduce latency and hallucination risks. To address these limitations, a hybrid framework is proposed. This system uses an orchestrator to coordinate PPO-trained reinforcement learning and PID control, with LLM common-sense reasoning applied throughout the framework. LLM reasoning is further employed iteratively to refine the RL reward function for dynamic driving environments. The proposed framework is evaluated in highly randomized CARLA scenarios under diverse environmental and traffic conditions. The results demonstrate the potential of integrating LLM-based reasoning with conventional autonomous driving methods while retaining structured control and safety mechanism.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất framework hybrid dùng LLM làm orchestrator kết hợp RL (PPO) và PID control cho xe tự lái, với LLM reasoning được dùng iterative để tinh chỉnh reward function, đánh giá trên simulator CARLA.
