papers.title: LLM-based Hardware Development with Hierarchical IRs and End-to-End Multi-Agent Workflow
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in software development, but their use in complex hardware design remains limited. This gap stems from both the scarcity of public hardware training data and the fundamentally different methodologies used in hardware design. In particular, applying LLMs to hardware requires more than direct RTL generation: the model must understand module boundaries, inter-module connections, and verification requirements. In this paper, we present an LLM-based hardware development framework with hierarchical intermediate representations (IRs) and an end-to-end multi-agent workflow. The core idea is to provide an abstraction of hardware design to LLMs through two structured IRs: Architectural Sketch, which captures module topology and interconnection, and Operational Specification, which defines per-module functionality and interfaces. Our framework uses these IRs to decompose a complex design into sub-modules, specify the per-block functionality, and derive how each module should be tested and verified. We incorporate a multi-agent debug loop in the framework, allowing agents to get the error feedback and control the debug details such as the signals to be probed for simulation. We evaluate our framework on Verilog-Eval benchmark, achieving a pass@5 rate of 95.5%, which surpasses current state-of-the-art LLM generation frameworks. To better assess performance on complex, realistic designs, we introduce a new case study spanning applications from general-purpose processors to digital signal processing systems. Experimental results indicate that such complex designs exceed the capabilities of existing approaches, whereas our framework is the only one capable of producing functional end-to-end design. Our generated RTL follows all industry-standard design rules, is lint-clean, functionally correct and fully synthesizable.
papers.llm_summary: Xây dựng framework LLM multi-agent cho thiết kế hardware (Verilog) sử dụng hierarchical intermediate representations, đạt 95.5% pass@5 trên Verilog-Eval.
papers.llm_reason: Có experiment tốt nhưng domain hardware design hoàn toàn xa rời content/business AI của solopreneur, insight gần như không áp dụng được.

papers.title: WeGR: Towards Unified Generative Retrieval via Behavior-aware Tokenization and Preference Alignment
papers.abstract: Generative retrieval (GR) offers a promising paradigm for industrial search by unifying candidate generation within an autoregressive framework. However, effectively leveraging user behaviors in industrial GR remains challenging: existing SID tokenization methods struggle to preserve collaborative signals while maintaining balanced codebook utilization, whereas reinforcement learning (RL) for prioritizing high-value candidates suffers from sparse rewards when generated SIDs fail to match positive items. To address these challenges, we propose WeGR, a unified GR framework with two complementary components. Specifically, the Collaborative and Collapse-free Tokenizer (CoCo-VAE) injects query-to-item and item-to-item collaborative signals into continuous representations before quantization, preserving behavioral information without disrupting codebook optimization. It further couples first-layer codebook refresh to reactivate underutilized codewords with fidelity anti-collapse regularization, which broadens gradient coverage over relevant codewords and penalizes collisions in deeper layers to yield behavior-aware SIDs with balanced utilization. For preference alignment, Dynamic Horizon Policy Optimization (DHPO) progressively expands reward evaluation and policy optimization horizons to alleviate reward sparsity, enabling coarse-to-fine preference learning from SID prefixes to complete items without auxiliary reward models. Extensive offline experiments validate that WeGR improves retrieval and ranking performance. Moreover, a six-week online A/B test on a large-scale e-commerce search platform achieves relative gains of 2.539% in orders, 1.508% in CTR, and 1.381% in CVR, while reducing CPU and GPU usage by 25.5% and 26.1%. These results highlight the effectiveness and efficiency of WeGR in industrial deployment, supporting multiple search scenarios and tens of millions of daily page views.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất WeGR, framework generative retrieval thống nhất cho search công nghiệp với tokenizer nhận diện hành vi người dùng và phương pháp alignment preference theo horizon động.
papers.llm_reason: Liên quan AI retrieval/RL nhưng rất chuyên sâu về industrial search, abstract bị cắt thiếu thông tin thực nghiệm, gần như không liên quan content/business/marketing cho solopreneur.

papers.title: Making Small Code LLMs More Efficient for Secure Code Review with Neuro-Symbolic Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: As AI coding assistants generate more code, the need to review it for security flaws grows. Existing approaches leave a gap: static analyzers identify program sites but offer little explanation, while language-model explanations can be difficult to verify. Small open-weight code models could make security review available without sending proprietary code to a hosted service. We study whether fine-tuning helps these models turn security evidence into explanations that developers and tools can check. We present secSemScan, which pairs a static analyzer with a locally deployable model that writes a schema-constrained security monologue naming program sites, assigning a CWE, and giving a machine-parseable verdict. We also introduce OGSM (Oracle-Grounded Security Monologue), a dataset of 1,993 C/C\texttt{++} functions covering 22 CWEs in the taint and lifetime families. Each record pairs a function with analyzer-derived or fix-diff-derived evidence and a monologue. We fine-tune three open-weight code models in two stages, first on the output format and then on the monologue content. Because evaluation prompts supply the verdict and evidence, our results measure how well models use that information, not whether they detect vulnerabilities independently. On 355 test records, fine-tuning raised Qwen2.5-Coder-7B's verdict accuracy from 4.8\% to 96.6\%; DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B reached 78.9\%, and StarCoder2-7B reached 43.7\%. Qwen2.5-Coder-7B cited 87.5\% of Tier~1 oracle sites, and every line it cited belonged to the oracle evidence. The results suggest that fine-tuning helps small models produce more structured, evidence-linked security reasoning.
papers.llm_summary: Fine-tune small code LLM (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B) với neuro-symbolic approach để viết security monologue cho code review, đạt 96.6% verdict accuracy trên dataset OGSM 1993 hàm C/C++.
papers.llm_reason: Có experiment cụ thể và dataset mới, nhưng domain secure code review rất xa nội dung content/business AI; ít actionable insight cho solopreneur.

papers.title: RES-MR: Risk-Aware Reasoning for Explainable and Safe Medication Recommendation
papers.abstract: Medication recommendations seek to deliver personalized drug combinations based on patients' clinical information, where ensuring transparent decision-making and personalized safety are of paramount importance. However, existing approaches predominantly operate as ``black boxes'', offering limited interpretability and hindering clinician trust. Furthermore, they typically rely on fixed, patient-agnostic safety constraints, neglecting the heterogeneity of risk tolerance across individuals, which poses significant risks to vulnerable populations. To address these gaps, we propose \textbf{RES-MR}, a novel Risk-aware Reasoning framework for Explainable and Safe Medication Recommendation using LLMs. RES-MR follows a two-stage training paradigm: (1) an explainable clinical reasoning distillation stage to elicit diagnostic capabilities by fine-tuning on synthesized reasoning trajectories, grounded in patient-specific knowledge from graph retrieval; and (2) a risk-aware policy optimization stage to dynamically balance therapeutic efficacy with personalized safety. This stage employs disentangled drug factors to construct patient-specific reference prototypes that capture desired therapeutic drug features and risk features to avoid. These prototypes enable risk boundary calibration and guide the model toward safe recommendations via reward shaping and clipping. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that RES-MR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in terms of accuracy, safety, and explainability. Our code and data are available at: https://github.com/wangcong2001/RES-MR.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất RES-MR, framework dùng LLM với reasoning giải thích được và tối ưu an toàn theo mức chịu rủi ro cá nhân hóa cho việc gợi ý phối hợp thuốc lâm sàng.

papers.title: ATLAS: A Multi-Agent Framework for Lifting Binary to Canonical Compiler IR
papers.abstract: Lifting stripped, heavily optimized binaries to a canonical, pre-optimization LLVM intermediate representation (IR) is essential for downstream security analysis and legacy software migration when source code is unavailable. However, aggressive compiler optimizations rewrite control and data flow, remove structural metadata, and introduce type-erased low-level idioms, causing current lifters to produce malformed or semantically divergent IR. We present ATLAS, a multi-agent framework designed to reconstruct formally valid and canonical LLVM IR from optimized disassembly.ATLAS combines (i) Structure-aware, region-level retrieval, which utilizes pseudo-probe attribution to align optimized instructions with canonical IR exemplars, and (ii) a collaborative refinement loop that closes the gap between probabilistic generation and deterministic compiler constraints. Concretely, a Lift agent generates an initial IR draft conditioned on retrieved exemplars, an Advisor agent interprets LLVM verifier/compilation diagnostics and static checks to propose localized repair actions, and a Validation agent applies the edits, re-runs toolchain verification and (when available) runtime checks, and feeds the resulting diagnostics back to the Advisor. The agents iterate until the IR is verifier-clean and behaviorally consistent, or a budget limit is reached. On HumanEval-Decompile and MBPP, ATLAS outperforms seven baselines on lifting LLVM IR, achieving 91.8% re-executability and 89.4% CFG similarity across ARM, x86-64, and RISC-V binaries. Moreover, our evaluation demonstrates that ATLAS also outperforms the Binary to C to IR pipelines in pointer-flow precision and downstream analyzability. By recovering a well-formed, machine-centric representation, ATLAS enables practical cross-ISA recompilation and verifiable binary-only migration workflows.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất ATLAS, multi-agent framework lift binary tối ưu sang canonical LLVM IR qua collaborative refinement loop (Lift-Advisor-Validation), đạt kết quả tốt trên HumanEval-Decompile và MBPP.

papers.title: Agent4RE: A Self-Refining Multi-agent Framework for End-to-End Software Requirements Engineering and Benchmarking
papers.abstract: Existing LLM-based approaches for software Requirements Engineering (RE) typically rely on basic prompting strategies or rudimentary agent collaboration, under-utilizing the full potential of multi-agent systems. Meanwhile, available datasets focus on isolated subtasks, such as requirements extraction, classification, and completeness detection, leaving the absence of an end-to-end RE benchmark that spans from requirements elicitation to generation. We present Agent4RE - a self-refining multi-agent RE system that orchestrates specialized agents and incorporates two iterative improvement loops. To support evaluation, we construct RE-E2E - a real-world dataset built from human-written requirement specifications, enabling end-to-end assessment of RE workflows. Building on this foundation, we further propose two enhanced Agent4RE versions that incorporate either autonomous self-refinement or structured human feedback, and analyze their strengths and limitations across different scenarios. Evaluation on 8 Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrates that all three Agent4RE variants consistently outperform a domain-context-augmented prompting baseline by average 8% in text-based metrics. The two enhanced variants achieve the highest LLM-as-a-judge and human ratings, surpassing two RE baselines by approximately 0.8 points on a four-point scale. This consistent performance establishes Agent4RE as a practical end-to-end RE solution for industrial environments.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất Agent4RE, hệ thống multi-agent self-refining cho end-to-end software requirements engineering, kèm dataset RE-E2E và benchmark trên 8 LLM, đạt cải thiện trung bình 8% so với baseline.
papers.llm_reason: Kiến trúc multi-agent với iterative improvement loops có thể làm nội dung về pattern thiết kế agent, nhưng domain requirements engineering quá chuyên biệt, ít liên quan business/content trực tiếp.

papers.title: BE-CTDE: Blockchain-Enabled Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Anomaly Detection and Token Economics
papers.abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning supports cooperative decision-making in Internet of Things systems, but strategic deviations can disrupt coordination and undermine confidence in the training process. This paper proposes Blockchain-Enabled Centralized Training and Decentralized Execution (BE-CTDE), which uses blockchain as an active training-management layer. A behavioral verifier compares executed trajectories with shared-policy recommendations; its flags drive a token mechanism combining slashing, burning, rewards, and compensation. Retained balances determine each agent's contribution to the global policy update, connecting auditable behavior to learning influence. We derive a one-round incentive condition that accounts for action-dependent compensation and the payoff from deviation, and a finite expected exclusion-time bound under explicit conditional detection and accounting assumptions, showing perfect detection is unnecessary. An exact finite-population capacity bound characterizes the limits of the population-relative detector. In multi-agent path finding experiments, BE-CTDE outperforms a state-of-the-art learning-based path planner with substantially higher success rates under attack, even when adversaries form the majority. It also outperforms partially defended baselines in all configurations, with collision rates up to 35% lower than under detection without economic consequences and up to 43% lower than under conventional stake slashing. Together, these results characterize how behavioral verification and token feedback can support accountable cooperative learning.
papers.llm_summary: Kết hợp blockchain với multi-agent reinforcement learning, dùng cơ chế token (slashing, burning, reward) để phát hiện hành vi lệch chuẩn và duy trì phối hợp trong hệ thống IoT.

papers.title: MA-JEPA: Joint-Embedding World Models for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: World models improve sample efficiency by training policies on imagined trajectories, but their usefulness depends on learning representations that capture the information needed for future control. We study whether self-supervised joint-embedding prediction (JEPA) can provide this learning signal for multi-agent reinforcement learning. We introduce MA-JEPA, a stochastic world model that replaces observation reconstruction with prediction of target representations, enabling model-based multi-agent reinforcement learning with centralized training and decentralized execution. A categorical latent state and a causal Transformer are trained with posterior and action-conditioned dynamics prediction objectives and are then used for actor-critic learning from latent imagination. A training-only joint predictor conditions on all agents' local states and actions to predict each agent's next local observation embedding. These predictions are passed through the same local posterior used during real interaction with a centralized critic that is used only for value learning, with execution remaining decentralized. Our experiments show that this architecture performs strongly on SMAC, matching or exceeding the strongest reported comparator mean win rate on four of eight evaluated maps.
papers.llm_summary: Giới thiệu MA-JEPA, dùng world model joint-embedding (JEPA) thay vì reconstruction để cải thiện sample efficiency cho multi-agent reinforcement learning.

papers.title: MA-UITD: Offline Multi-Agent Reward Inference for Characterizing Continuous Social Behavior
papers.abstract: Multi-agent inverse reinforcement learning offers a powerful framework not only for imitation learning but also for understanding the neural computations supporting social interactions and decision-making. Inferring rewards from interacting agents is challenging because observed choices reflect both personal preferences and expectations about others. Existing methods often require additional environment interaction, repeated policy optimization as an inner loop, or restrictive assumptions about environment dynamics and action spaces, limiting their applicability to fixed behavioral datasets. We introduce Multi-Agent Unilateral Inverse Temporal Difference Learning (MA-UITD), an offline method for inferring explicit agent-specific rewards from joint demonstrations in continuous-state environments with either discrete or bounded continuous actions. Its core idea is to represent the long-term consequences of each agent's own actions through belief-conditioned successor features that average over other agents' behavior. Shared reward features and agent-specific preference vectors connect these unilateral values to the target reward function, while inverse temporal-difference consistency and noise-contrastive behavioral learning enable inference without known dynamics or an inner policy-optimization loop. Across simulated cooperative, competitive, and general-sum tasks, MA-UITD outperforms baselines in discrete-action settings and infers behaviorally compatible reward profiles in continuous-action settings. When applied to experimentally collected social-foraging trajectories, MA-UITD inferred distinct spatial and interaction-dependent reward structures for leaders and followers, providing a quantitative characterization of latent behavioral objectives that may be relevant for understanding the neural computations underlying social behavior.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất phương pháp offline suy luận phần thưởng riêng cho từng agent trong hệ thống đa tác tử từ dữ liệu hành vi chung, dùng belief-conditioned successor features và inverse temporal-difference consistency.

papers.title: Semantics Delivery Network: Rethinking Web Retrieval Infrastructure for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly ground their answers in proprietary data and live web content through both single-shot retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and multi-turn agentic search. Yet the web path they use was built for human readers: search services return URLs and snippets ranked by generic relevance, and content delivery networks (CDNs) cache URL-addressed objects without knowing which passage an agent needs. LLMs instead consume short, semantically coherent passages - hereafter, chunks - selected for downstream utility rather than similarity alone, retrieve statefully across reasoning turns, and, as uncoordinated streams, repeatedly fetch, clean, chunk, and embed the same content. We argue that semantic chunk retrieval should become a first-class network-delivery abstraction, and propose the Semantics Delivery Network (SemDN): an origin-authorized, hierarchical substrate that indexes, searches, and caches web content at chunk granularity, serving clients and origins alike. SemDN is more than finer-grained caching: it must estimate missing or stale evidence without an explicit miss signal, let clients choose retrieval representations that origins need not see, and share state among clients with the same representation. Preliminary results show that page-first retrieval processes two to three orders of magnitude more content than agents consume, that agentic queries exhibit task-local chunk reuse invisible to URL caches, and that chunk delivery improves answer quality per context token. We organize an open research agenda around shareable retrieval state, hierarchical caching and refresh under coverage risk, and deployability, including incentives, privacy, and verifiability. Our code is available at: https://github.com/sarendis56/SemDN_HotNets26
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất Semantics Delivery Network (SemDN) — hạ tầng mạng mới phục vụ retrieval theo semantic chunk cho LLM agent, thay vì retrieval theo URL như hiện tại, cho thấy page-first retrieval xử lý nhiều hơn 100-1000 lần nội dung so với nhu cầu thực tế của agent.

papers.title: Verifying Neural Networks with Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Formal verification can play a key role in ensuring the reliability of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) deployed in safety-critical systems. Modern DNN verifiers employ a branch-and-bound framework, which alternates between branching (splitting into smaller subproblems) and bounding (pruning subproblems) to efficiently explore the verification space. However, existing branching heuristics make greedy decisions based on static scoring functions. They do not anticipate long-term efficiency or leverage the growing availability of verification data to improve performance. This work introduces RSB, a reinforcement learning framework that learns to refine baseline branching heuristics. It trains an actor-critic architecture to maximize cumulative future rewards rather than immediate scores. The actor generates attention weights from observations of raw neuron features and learned graph embeddings, which rescale baseline heuristic scores to guide neuron branching. Evaluation on 600 challenging instances demonstrates that RSB consistently outperforms state-of-the-art branching heuristics, solving 11% more instances while reducing branch exploration by 50%.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất RSB, framework reinforcement learning để học heuristic branching cho formal verification mạng neural, giải thêm 11% instances và giảm 50% exploration so với SOTA.
papers.llm_reason: RL và neural verification hoàn toàn xa LLM/agent/content/business, dù có experiment tốt nhưng không liên quan gì đến solopreneur làm content AI.

papers.title: CAT-RAG: Improving Secure Code Generation with Category-Aware Agentic Retrieval
papers.abstract: Despite rapid progress in LLM-based code generation, security vulnerabilities remain widespread, and retrieval-augmented code generation (RACG) can further amplify risk when retrieved knowledge is verbose or vulnerable to poisoning. Existing secure RACG approaches inject security knowledge at a fine-grained vulnerability level, causing prompt overhead and diluted model attention when a query implicates multiple related weaknesses. We propose CAT-RAG, an agentic security category-aware retrieval-augmented code generation framework. CAT-RAG performs adaptive category selection via an LLM as a categorizer agent and operates either as a standalone security layer or as a drop-in add-on to RACG pipelines, requiring no modification to the underlying model. We replace CWE-level retrieval with compact, language-specific security categories. These categories provide a higher-level abstraction over individual CWE weaknesses, organizing them by the security concern they share, such as Input Validation and Injection Attacks, rather than merely grouping related entries. Each category consolidates best practices and secure code examples into a single, prompt-efficient representation. We perform a comprehensive evaluation across CyberSecEval, CodeGuard+, and HumanEval. On CyberSecEval, CAT-RAG nearly doubles the secure code generation improvement over the state of the art (23.57% vs. 12.11%) while reducing token overhead by 41.71%.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất CAT-RAG, framework agentic retrieval-augmented code generation dùng security category-aware retrieval thay vì CWE-level, cải thiện secure code generation gần gấp đôi so với SOTA (23.57% vs 12.11%) trên CyberSecEval.
papers.llm_reason: Kết quả benchmark ấn tượng nhưng chuyên sâu về secure code generation, quá hẹp và xa nội dung content/business AI mà solopreneur đang làm.

papers.title: Multi-AUV Ad-hoc network-based Target Tracking: A Value Gradient Guidance Multi-Agent Diffusion Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.abstract: Multi-AUV ad-hoc network-based target tracking requires networked autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) to cooperatively track maneuvering targets under constrained acoustic communication, dynamic topology, and uncertain ocean disturbances. Although multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) enables decentralized coordination through centralized training, existing methods suffer from high-dimensional joint state-action modeling, noise-sensitive policy generation, leading to unstable training and degraded tracking. To address these issues, we propose VGG-MADiffRL, a value-gradient-guided multi-agent diffusion RL algorithm, and MDCA, a diffusion?based hierarchical control architecture. Leveraging underwater mission characteristics, we model sonar detection mechanisms and ocean current disturbances, formulating cooperative tracking for multi-AUV ad-hoc networks as an MDP. The proposed MDCA constitutes a three-tier closed-loop control framework: a global intelligent control layer, a local online training layer, and a physical action execution layer. This structure enables synergistic optimization across task allocation, local decision processes, and execution feedback. Within MDCA, the local online training layer is the policy learning framework; VGG-MADiffRL builds on diffusion policies and incorporates value gradients to guide action generation in the reverse denoising process, steering the generated actions towards higher expected returns. It employs twin value networks with joint optimization and soft target updates to mitigate overestimation and training oscillations, promoting more stable convergence. Experimental results show that VGG-MADiffRL consistently achieves faster convergence, higher tracking accuracy, and smoother training dynamics in cooperative tracking scenarios, validating its effectiveness and practical engineering value in dynamic underwater settings.
papers.llm_summary: VGG-MADiffRL dùng multi-agent diffusion reinforcement learning có value-gradient để đàn AUV hợp tác tracking mục tiêu trong mạng ad-hoc dưới nước.
papers.llm_reason: Là MARL/diffusion RL chuyên biệt, không LLM/agent content cốt lõi (10), experiment thật nhưng hẹp dưới nước (14), gần như không liên quan business/content (2) và ít insight dùng cho creator (3).

papers.title: MetaPermit: Scalable and Auditable Access Control for AI Agents via LLM-Inferred Meta-Attributes
papers.abstract: The rise of autonomous AI agents equipped with tools has introduced significant security risks, ranging from unintended tool misuse to adversarial manipulation through Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) attacks. In practice, deployed agent systems such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code protect tool invocations through a combination of coarse-grained permission rules and LLM-based judgments about individual proposed actions. Both components, however, have important limitations: static policies must anticipate possible user intents and therefore do not scale to open-ended tasks, while LLM-driven authorization supports dynamic decisions but produces inconsistent outcomes and remains vulnerable to targeted IPI attacks. To provide scalable and more consistent authorization, we propose MetaPermit, a policy-based tool access-control framework that decouples semantic inference from security enforcement. By analyzing agent-user interactions, we derive a compact, task-independent set of meta-attributes that capture the relationships among the user's intent, the execution context, and the proposed tool call. These meta-attributes allow MetaPermit to authorize tool use without enumerating user intents. At runtime, an LLM infers the meta-attribute values for each proposed tool call, while a fixed policy evaluates these values to allow or deny the call, making each decision auditable through the inferred values and the applied policy rule. We evaluate MetaPermit on the AgentDojo and AgentDyn benchmarks, across seven task suites and five attack methods, using two widely deployed open-weight LLMs. The results show that MetaPermit produces 31% more consistent authorization decisions than LLM-driven authorization and outperforms the state-of-the-art defenses CaMeL and IPIGuard in both task completion, with improvements of up to 109%, and robustness to IPI attacks, with no malicious tool calls executed.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất MetaPermit, framework access control cho AI agent dùng LLM suy luận meta-attributes từ interaction context, tách biệt semantic inference khỏi security enforcement để authorization scalable và auditable.
papers.llm_reason: Liên quan agent tool-use nhưng tập trung vào access control policy — quá kỹ thuật và bảo mật, ít giá trị content hay actionable insight cho solopreneur làm content AI.

papers.title: ICEGR: An Intent-Coherent End-to-End Generative Retrieval Framework for E-commerce Search
papers.abstract: Generative Retrieval (GR) is promising for e-commerce search, yet existing methods struggle to maintain query-intent consistency throughout the training pipeline. First, semantic ID (SID) construction based on static product information limits the ability of SIDs to encode product-intent associations. Second, although supervised fine-tuning (SFT) learns product-SID mappings across the catalog, low-exposure products still lack real query-intent supervision because query-to-SID training relies solely on online logs, resulting in poor retrieval performance for these products. Third, business-oriented preference optimization may favor popular or high-value products over those that best match the query intent, weakening query-product relevance. To address these issues, we propose ICEGR, an Intent-Coherent End-to-End Generative Retrieval Framework for E-commerce Search that integrates query intent consistently throughout the GR training pipeline. ICEGR comprises three components: (1) Intent-Aware SID Construction incorporates query-intent signals into SID construction, enabling SIDs to capture search intent beyond static product information; (2) Synthetic Query-Enhanced Unified SFT unifies multiple SFT tasks under the query-to-SID objective and augments sparse supervision from online logs with synthetic queries, providing complementary query-intent supervision for low-exposure products; and (3) Relevance-Calibrated Preference Optimization integrates query-product relevance and business signals into a margin-adaptive preference objective, preserving query intent while enabling business preference learning. Offline results show that ICEGR improves Recall@20 by 21.7% and NDCG@20 by 26.6% over the baseline. Deployed as an end-to-end generative retrieval pathway in Baidu E-commerce Search, ICEGR achieves relative improvements of 3.52% in CTR, 15.96% in order volume, and 7.53% in GMV in an A/B test.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất ICEGR, framework generative retrieval end-to-end cho e-commerce search, tích hợp query intent xuyên suốt pipeline qua intent-aware SID construction, synthetic query augmentation và preference optimization.
papers.llm_reason: Thuần về e-commerce search retrieval, không liên quan LLM agent hay content creation; chỉ có giá trị nhỏ nếu solopreneur quan tâm tối ưu tìm kiếm sản phẩm.

papers.title: AGATE: Provenance-Based Runtime Defense Against Compositional Attacks on LLM Agents
papers.abstract: LLM agents can produce harmful effects through sequences of ordinary operations. Judging such actions requires establishing both the authority that permits them and the origin of the data they carry. We present AGATE, an authorization and data-provenance gate at instrumented agent-harness boundaries. Operator declarations and host approval events ground authorization; delegated actions are constrained by grants that bind to exact parameters, expire, and permit a limited number of uses. Source registration connects observed inputs to subsequent transfers, while an effect ledger tracks repeated requests. Deterministic checks make decisions without an LLM in the decision path and retain their grounds with execution evidence for forensic replay. Adapters integrate three production harnesses -- DeepSeek Harness, OpenCode, and OpenClaw -- without modifying host code, translating each host's native observation and veto points into a single shared gate interface; the judgment core is identical in all three, and only enforcement depth differs. Our evaluation combines 153 exercised attack-chain records with deployment, utility, and reconstruction experiments. The deployment observations expose how tool declarations and data checks govern business actions, including a bypass through parameter rewriting. Six of eleven benign file-processing scenarios contain denial events, revealing the utility cost of content-based provenance policies. Across 252 runs on 63 sanitized scenarios, replay agrees with live graph projections for all 63 scenarios on each of two platforms. These results establish the feasibility of provenance-based runtime judgment and identify content transformation, legitimate reuse, and observation coverage as concrete limits.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất AGATE, hệ thống defense runtime dựa trên provenance chống compositional attack trên LLM agent, tích hợp vào 3 production harness (DeepSeek, OpenCode, OpenClaw) với deterministic checks không cần LLM trong decision path.
papers.llm_reason: Rất kỹ thuật về agent security defense, data thực nghiệm có nhưng domain quá niche, gần như không có insight actionable cho người làm content/business AI.

papers.title: The Voice on the Line
papers.abstract: A transcriber listening through one microphone also hears everyone near it. We train causal voice isolators: masking transformers of 140M, 243M and 374M parameters, 20 ms of latency, enrolling the caller from the call itself. Short evaluation windows hide two failures that real calls expose: forgetting the caller when another voice talks alone for a while, and damaging a caller who is alone. Long calls with turns, memory beyond the attention window, real headset crosstalk and drifting caller levels address both, but each trades one against the other. WavLM-Large's own weights, made causal and trained with the model, move the trade: M with them (555M parameters) lowers the error on our development sets from 11.44% to 10.55%; a student trained from scratch to imitate WavLM does not, and w2v-BERT 2.0 and Whisper's encoder, pre-trained on far more audio, help less or not at all. A lone caller loses most at the start of a recording: no training call opened with someone already talking. Training on windows cut from longer calls lowers the error on clean development calls from 3.92% to 2.96%; this is our release. Live, the release makes 16.13% word errors on 60 s AMI windows, against 23.66% for VoxLock, the strongest open isolator, and 10.19% on its own AMI windows, against 11.71%; it is level on Krisp's benchmark (5.74% against 5.63%), and a caller who is alone still loses more words than with VoxLock (5.58% against 2.92% on clean test calls). Distilled into 22.1M parameters without WavLM, it runs live on one CPU thread inside a LiveKit agent, at 33% of a core per call in 20 ms frames, with 10.66% error on our development sets (the release 10.49%). We open-source the release and this CPU model, with a LiveKit plugin, at https://huggingface.co/collections/Scicom-intl/voice-isolator.
papers.llm_summary: Huấn luyện causal voice isolation transformers (140M-555M parameters, 20ms latency) để tách giọng caller trong cuộc gọi thực, đạt WER 10.19% trên benchmark AMI, cạnh tranh với VoxLock và Krisp.
papers.llm_reason: Là audio processing chuyên sâu, không liên quan LLM/agent; có thể hữu ích nhỏ nếu solopreneur cần tool xử lý âm thanh cho podcast/video nhưng bản thân paper không cung cấp insight actionable đó.

papers.title: AIRRI: Towards a Human-Readable, Machine-Resistant Reading Interface
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of image-to-text extraction systems and large language models (LLMs) poses new challenges for educational assessment by making assignment materials easy to transcribe and solve with minimal human effort. To address this problem, we present AIRRI (Artificial Intelligence Resilient Reading Interface), a framework for generating machine-resistant educational content, a dataset of higher-education assignments for evaluation, and an initial evaluation of the human readability of AIRRI machine-resistant text designs. AIRRI employs two categories of machine-resistance techniques. First, AIRRI applies image transformations including character spacing, word spacing, line spacing, character opacity variation, stripe overlays, and image noise. Second, AIRRI applies decision-based adversarial attacks: RayS, SurFree, and ADBA. We evaluate AIRRI against three image-to-text systems: Tesseract, EasyOCR, and the transformer-based GOT-OCR2 model. Our results show that AIRRI substantially degrades automated text extraction performance. AIRRI increased character error rates for EasyOCR (6.9% to 55.9%), Tesseract (2.3% to 100.0%), and GOT-OCR2 (30.7% to 48.1%). Word error rates increased for EasyOCR (24.9% to 96.7%) and Tesseract (10.7% to 100.0%). Among the evaluated decision-based attacks, ADBA consistently produced the largest degradation in image-to-text performance, while RayS and SurFree produced more moderate reductions. EasyOCR and Tesseract were generally more susceptible to both image-based and adversarial perturbations than the transformer-based GOT-OCR2 model. Our findings suggest that AIRRI can significantly reduce the reliability of image-to-text-to-LLM workflows, increasing the effort required for AI-assisted assignment completion.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất AIRRI, framework tạo nội dung giáo dục chống AI đọc được bằng cách kết hợp image transformations và adversarial attacks (RayS, SurFree, ADBA) để degrading hiệu suất OCR systems.
papers.llm_reason: Hoàn toàn không liên quan AI/LLM/agent content creation hay business — thuộc về adversarial OCR trong giáo dục, không có giá trị thực tiễn cho profile solopreneur này.
